lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Pre-reading

  • Q: Q1. Why did non-Muslims trust Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him)?
    Ans: Non-Muslims trusted Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) because he was always truthful, honest and just. Even before Prophethood he remained away from the moral degeneration of society, opposed oppression and injustice, and gave every person his or her due without favour, so people of all faiths trusted his word and his decisions.
  • Q: Q2. How did Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) set high and noble ideals for all mankind?
    Ans: He set high and noble ideals by his own practical example. He based the justice system on the principle of giving a person his or her due, whatever his or her stature might be. He decided every case on merit, with justice and fairness, without fear or favour, even when a case was against his own interest or the interest of those near and dear to him.
  • Q: Q3. How can people achieve perfection in the moral, spiritual and social areas of life?
    Ans: People can achieve perfection in the moral, spiritual and social areas of life by following the commands of Allah and the excellent pattern of the life of Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him). They should stand firm for justice, speak the truth, give everyone his or her due, and never let personal desires, hatred or relationships make them unjust.

Glossary — Word Meanings (as printed in the book)

  • Q: What does 'apostleship' mean?
    Ans: Apostleship: a person who strongly believes in a policy or an idea and tries to make other people believe in it (as printed in the glossary).
  • Q: What does 'degeneration' mean?
    Ans: Degeneration: the process of becoming worse or less acceptable in quality or condition.
  • Q: What does 'implementation' mean?
    Ans: Implementation: the act of making something that has been officially decided to happen or be used.
  • Q: What does 'witness' mean?
    Ans: Witness: a person who sees something happen and is able to describe it to other people.
  • Q: What does 'evidence' mean?
    Ans: Evidence: the facts, signs or objects that make you believe that something is true.
  • Q: What does 'transcend' mean?
    Ans: Transcend: to be or go beyond the usual limits of something.
  • Q: What does 'guilty' mean?
    Ans: Guilty: feeling ashamed because you have done something that you know is wrong or have not done something that you should have done.
  • Q: What does 'emphatically' mean?
    Ans: Emphatically: in a very clear way that involves speaking with force.
  • Q: What does 'magnitude' mean?
    Ans: Magnitude: the great size or importance of something; the degree to which something is large or important.
  • Q: What does 'intercede' mean?
    Ans: Intercede: to speak to somebody in order to persuade them to have pity on somebody else or to help settle an argument.
  • Q: What does 'investigation' mean?
    Ans: Investigation: an official examination of the facts about a situation, crime, etc.
  • Q: What does 'ignorance' mean?
    Ans: Ignorance: a lack of knowledge or information about something.
  • Q: What does 'fairness' mean?
    Ans: Fairness: the quality of treating people equally or in a way that is reasonable.
  • Q: What does 'barrier' mean?
    Ans: Barrier: an object like a fence that prevents people from moving forward from one place to another.

Comprehension A — Answer the Following Questions

  • Q: Q1. Describe an event of justice from the life of Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) from the text.
    Ans: Once a Quraish woman was found guilty of stealing. Some people wanted to save her from punishment to protect the honour of the family of Quraish, and they asked Hazrat Asama bin Zaid, who was very dear to the Rasool (peace be upon him), to intercede on her behalf. Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) became very angry and refused, saying that Bani Israel was ruined because they applied the law to the poor and forgave the rich. In this way he showed that the law is equal for everyone, rich or poor.
  • Q: Q2. What is referred to as 'A piece of fire' by Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him)?
    Ans: Gains made by deceiving a judge to get a positive decision are referred to as 'a piece of fire' by Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him). In his system of justice a decision is made according to evidence, so false witnessing and the presentation of unfounded evidence were emphatically forbidden.
  • Q: Q3. Why was an inquiry initiated by Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) while resolving the land dispute?
    Ans: During his time a cottage was built on a piece of land belonging to two brothers, and after their death the heirs disputed the ownership of the cottage. Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) assigned Huzayfa bin Yemin to handle the case. An inquiry was initiated so that the case could be decided according to evidence: Huzayfa went to the cottage for discovery and investigation, took statements from various people and evidences from witnesses, and then presented his decision for approval. The inquiry made sure that no wrong was made right with his decision.
  • Q: Q4. How does the Holy Quran emphasize justice?
    Ans: The Holy Quran emphasizes justice again and again. In Surat an-Nisa (4:135) Allah commands believers to stand firm for justice as witnesses for Allah, even if it is against themselves, their parents or close relatives, rich or poor, and not to let their desires make them deviate from justice. In Surah al-Maida (5:8) believers are told to maintain justice even with their enemies and not to let hatred of a people incite them to act unjustly, because being just is nearer to righteousness.
  • Q: Q5. What is the main idea of the lesson?
    Ans: The main idea of the lesson is that Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) established a perfect system of justice based on the commands of Allah. He gave every person his or her due without fear or favour, decided cases on evidence and merit, and treated the rich and the poor, friend and foe, equally. His life is an excellent pattern of justice for all mankind.
  • Q: Q6. What role can justice play in our lives?
    Ans: Justice can bring peace, trust and harmony in our lives and in society. When everyone gets his or her due, the weak are protected from the powerful, disputes are settled fairly and no one is oppressed. A just society progresses, while injustice destroys nations, as it destroyed Bani Israel. Justice also makes our personal dealings honest and earns the pleasure of Allah.

Comprehension B — Agree or Disagree with Reasons

  • Q: Q1. 'We live in a fair and just society.' Do you agree or disagree? Give a reason.
    Ans: I disagree, because in our society the powerful often escape punishment while the weak suffer, and people sometimes get their rights only through influence or money. However, we can make our society fair and just by following the example of Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) and treating everyone equally.
  • Q: Q2. 'It is important to treat others with justice and fairness.' Do you agree or disagree? Give a reason.
    Ans: I agree, because treating others with justice and fairness creates trust, peace and harmony in society. The Holy Quran also commands us to be just even with our enemies, and the Holy Prophet (peace be upon him) decided every case with justice, without fear or favour.
  • Q: Q3. 'Revenge can sometimes be justified.' Do you agree or disagree? Give a reason.
    Ans: I disagree, because revenge is personal and unjust, and it destroys the rule of law. Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) clearly said, 'The revenge of the father cannot be taken on his son.' Punishment should be given only to the guilty person, through a fair legal process, and not as revenge on anyone else.
  • Q: Q4. 'There is justice and fairness at my school.' Do you agree or disagree? Give a reason.
    Ans: I agree, because at my school merit is given in every matter: marks are awarded according to the students' work, prizes and positions go to those who deserve them, and the teachers treat all students equally without favouring anyone.

mcqs.q: Why did non-Muslims trust Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him)?

He was the richest merchant in Makkah
He belonged to the tribe of Quraish

mcqs.q: What did Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) call 'a piece of fire'?

False evidence given in a court
Gains made by deceiving a judge to get a positive decision

mcqs.why: The notes say he assigned Huzayfa bin Yemin to handle the case of the cottage built on land belonging to two brothers, whose heirs later disputed its ownership.

So that the cottage could be sold quickly
So that the brothers could divide the land equally
So that the witnesses could be punished
mcqs.why: The notes explain that the inquiry was initiated so the case could be decided according to evidence, after discovery, investigation and statements from witnesses.

mcqs.q: According to Surat an-Nisa (4:135), believers must stand firm for justice even if it is against whom?
options: Themselves, their parents or close relatives
mcqs.why: The notes quote Surat an-Nisa (4:135): believers must stand firm for justice as witnesses for Allah even if it is against themselves, their parents or close relatives.

mcqs.q: What does Surah al-Maida (5:8) teach about justice towards enemies?
options: Enemies should never be treated justly
Justice is only for close relatives
Believers must maintain justice even with enemies and not let hatred make them unjust
Hatred of a people justifies revenge
mcqs.why: The notes say Surah al-Maida (5:8) tells believers to maintain justice even with their enemies and not let hatred incite them to act unjustly, because being just is nearer to righteousness.

mcqs.q: What does the word 'intercede' mean in the glossary of the lesson?

To feel ashamed after doing wrong
To go beyond the usual limits of something
To speak to somebody to persuade them to have pity on somebody else or help settle an argument
mcqs.why: The glossary in the notes defines 'intercede' as speaking to somebody in order to persuade them to have pity on somebody else or to help settle an argument.

mcqs.q: What does the word 'evidence' mean in the glossary of the lesson?
options: The facts, signs or objects that make you believe that something is true
A person who sees something happen
The quality of treating people equally
The great size or importance of something
mcqs.why: The glossary in the notes defines 'evidence' as the facts, signs or objects that make you believe that something is true, and decisions were made according to evidence.

mcqs.q: What is the main idea of the lesson 'The Holy Prophet's Justice'?
options: Justice should favour the rich and powerful
Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) established a perfect system of justice, giving every person his or her due without fear or favour
Laws should be changed for noble families

mcqs.why: The notes state the main idea: he established a perfect system of justice based on Allah's commands, decided cases on evidence and merit, and treated rich and poor, friend and foe, equally.

Vocabulary C — Silent Letters

  • Q: Q1. Underline the silent letter in 'climb'.
    Ans: Climb — the letter 'b' is silent. The word is pronounced 'clime'.
  • Q: Q2. Underline the silent letter in 'bridge'.
    Ans: Bridge — the letter 'd' is silent. The word is pronounced 'brij'.
  • Q: Q3. Underline the silent letter in 'edge'.
    Ans: Edge — the letter 'd' is silent. The word is pronounced 'ej'.
  • Q: Q4. Underline the silent letter in 'comb'.
    Ans: Comb — the letter 'b' is silent. The word is pronounced 'cohm'.
  • Q: Q5. Underline the silent letter in 'subtle'.
    Ans: Subtle — the letter 'b' is silent. The word is pronounced 'sut-l'.
  • Q: Q6. Underline the silent letter in 'debt'.
    Ans: Debt — the letter 'b' is silent. The word is pronounced 'det'.
  • Q: Q7. Underline the silent letter in 'doubt'.
    Ans: Doubt — the letter 'b' is silent. The word is pronounced 'dout'.

Vocabulary D — Words Divided into Syllables

  • Q: Q1. Divide 'orderly' into syllables.
    Ans: Orderly — or-der-ly (3 syllables).
  • Q: Q2. Divide 'disagree' into syllables.

  • Q: Q5. Divide 'gardener' into syllables.
    Ans: Gardener — gar-den-er (3 syllables).
  • Q: Q6. Divide 'silently' into syllables.
    Ans: Silently — si-lent-ly (3 syllables).
  • Q: Q7. Divide 'lovingly' into syllables.
    Ans: Lovingly — lov-ing-ly (3 syllables).

Grammar — Long and Short Vowel Sounds

  • Q: Q1. Tell whether the vowel in bold is long or short: 'coat' (oa).
    Ans: Coat — the vowel sound 'oa' is long (long O).
  • Q: Q2. Tell whether the vowel in bold is long or short: 'odd' (o).
    Ans: Odd — the vowel 'o' is short (short O).
  • Q: Q3. Tell whether the vowel in bold is long or short: 'program' (o).
    Ans: Program — the vowel 'o' is long (long O).
  • Q: Q4. Tell whether the vowel in bold is long or short: 'soda' (o).
    Ans: Soda — the vowel 'o' is long (long O).
  • Q: Q5. Tell whether the vowel in bold is long or short: 'psycho' (o).
    Ans: Psycho — the vowel 'o' at the end is long (long O).
  • Q: Q6. Tell whether the vowel in bold is long or short: 'use' (u).
    Ans: Use — the vowel 'u' is long (long U).
  • Q: Q7. Tell whether the vowel in bold is long or short: 'stun' (u).
    Ans: Stun — the vowel 'u' is short (short U).
  • Q: Q8. Tell whether the vowel in bold is long or short: 'refuse' (u).
    Ans: Refuse — the vowel 'u' is long (long U).
  • Q: Q9. Tell whether the vowel in bold is long or short: 'ugly' (u).
    Ans: Ugly — the vowel 'u' is short (short U).

Grammar — Word Stress (Using a Dictionary)

  • Q: Q1. Find the word stress in 'media'.
    Ans: Media — stress on the first syllable: ME-di-a.
  • Q: Q2. Find the word stress in 'bacteria'.
    Ans: Bacteria — stress on the second syllable: bac-TE-ri-a.
  • Q: Q3. Find the word stress in 'ingredient'.
    Ans: Ingredient — stress on the second syllable: in-GRE-di-ent.
  • Q: Q4. Find the word stress in 'patient'.
    Ans: Patient — stress on the first syllable: PA-tient.
  • Q: Q5. Find the word stress in 'ancient'.
    Ans: Ancient — stress on the first syllable: AN-cient.
  • Q: Q6. Find the word stress in 'mysterious'.
    Ans: Mysterious — stress on the second syllable: mys-TE-ri-ous.

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary A — Meanings and Parts of Speech

  • Q: Q1. 'opposed' — meaning and part of speech.
    Ans: Opposed means to disagree with and try to stop something, or to be against something. Part of speech: verb (v.), as used in the lesson: 'He opposed oppression and injustice in his youth.'
  • Q: Q2. 'oppression' — meaning and part of speech.
    Ans: Oppression means cruel and unjust treatment of people, or the exercise of power in a cruel and unfair way. Part of speech: noun (n.).
  • Q: Q3. 'approval' — meaning and part of speech.
    Ans: Approval means official permission or agreement for something, or a feeling of liking something. Part of speech: noun (n.), as in the lesson: 'presented his decision to Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) for his approval.'
  • Q: Q4. 'decision' — meaning and part of speech.
    Ans: Decision means a choice or judgement made after thinking about something. Part of speech: noun (n.).
  • Q: Q5. 'heir' — meaning and part of speech.
    Ans: Heir means a person who receives money, property or a title when the owner dies. Part of speech: noun (n.), as in the lesson: 'The heirs disputed ownership of the cottage.'
  • Q: Q6. 'adopted' — meaning and part of speech.
    Ans: Adopted means taken up and used, or legally taken into one's family as one's own child. Part of speech: verb (v.), the past form of 'adopt'.
  • Q: Q7. 'distinction' — meaning and part of speech.
    Ans: Distinction means a clear difference between two or more things, or a special honour given for excellence. Part of speech: noun (n.).

Vocabulary B — Synonyms (from a Thesaurus)

  • Q: Q1. Give a synonym of 'unfriendly'.
    Ans: Unfriendly — hostile, unkind, cold.
  • Q: Q2. Give a synonym of 'opposing'.
    Ans: Opposing — against, conflicting, contrary.
  • Q: Q3. Give a synonym of 'danger'.
    Ans: Danger — risk, hazard, peril.
  • Q: Q4. Give a synonym of 'approval'.
    Ans: Approval — consent, permission, agreement.
  • Q: Q5. Give a synonym of 'false'.
    Ans: False — untrue, wrong, incorrect.
  • Q: Q6. Give a synonym of 'resolve'.
    Ans: Resolve — settle, solve, decide.
  • Q: Q7. Give a synonym of 'issue'.
    Ans: Issue — matter, problem, topic.

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Writing A — Mind Map and Summary of the Lesson

  • Q: Q1. Complete the mind map of 'Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) — Justice'.
    Ans: Central idea: Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) — Justice. Idea 1: Opposition to injustice — Sub-idea (before Prophethood): he remained away from the moral degeneration of society and joined Hulf-ul-Fudul, the Pact of Social Justice, for fair dealing; Sub-idea (after Prophethood): he based the justice system on giving every person his or her due. Idea 2: Justice according to evidence — Sub-idea: the land dispute was investigated by Huzayfa bin Yemin through discovery, witness statements and evidence; Sub-idea: false witnessing and unfounded evidence were forbidden, and gains by deceiving a judge were called 'a piece of fire'. Idea 3: Equality before the law — Sub-idea: he refused intercession for the Quraish woman guilty of stealing and said Bani Israel was ruined for punishing the poor and forgiving the rich; Sub-idea: he said the revenge of the father cannot be taken on his son, and decided every case on merit without fear or favour.
  • Q: Q2. Write down the summary of the lesson 'Hazrat Muhammad's (peace be upon him) Justice'.
    Ans: Summary: The lesson tells us that Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) followed Allah's command to stand firm for justice even against oneself and one's relatives. Justice was in his nature from childhood; he opposed oppression and joined the Pact of Social Justice, Hulf-ul-Fudul. Before Islam the Arabs had no sound written law and the weak were usually found guilty, but he based justice on giving everyone his or her due. In the land dispute he ordered a full inquiry by Huzayfa bin Yemin and decided the case on evidence. He forbade false witnessing and called gains obtained by deceiving a judge 'a piece of fire'. As head of the state of Madinah he decided all cases on merit; he refused to spare the Quraish woman guilty of stealing and declared that revenge for a father's crime cannot be taken on his son. His life is an excellent pattern of justice for all mankind.

Writing B — Specific Words, Vivid Verbs and Modifiers in the Second Paragraph

  • Q: Q1. Read the second paragraph of the lesson carefully and underline the specific words, vivid verbs and modifiers.
    Ans: In the second paragraph ('Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) abided by Allah's commands, even before he was entrusted with the duty of apostleship...'), the specific words are: Allah's commands, duty of apostleship, justice, nucleus, divine training, moral degeneration, oppression, injustice, youth, Pact of Social Justice, Hulf-ul-Fudul, fair commercial dealing, pre-Islamic Makkah. The vivid verbs are: abided, entrusted, instilled, remained, opposed, joined, formed. The modifiers are: even (adverb), as a result of divine training, moral (adjective), social (adjective), fair (adjective), pre-Islamic (adjective).

Writing C — Paragraph on 'Patience of Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him)'

  • Q: Q1. Write a simple and unified paragraph of about 50 to 60 words on 'Patience of Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him)' using a clear topic sentence, specific words, vivid verbs and modifiers.
    Ans: The unmatched patience of Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) shines brightly in every hardship of his noble life. Cruel enemies mocked him, pelted stones at him in Taif and blocked his peaceful mission, yet he calmly forgave them and sincerely prayed for their guidance. His gentle endurance teaches us true strength and mercy.

mcqs.q: What is the central idea of the mind map in the Writing section?
options: Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) — Justice
mcqs.why: The notes give the mind map's central idea as 'Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) — Justice', with branches on opposition to injustice, justice according to evidence and equality before the law.

mcqs.why: The summary in the notes states that before Islam the Arabs had no sound written law and the weak were usually found guilty, while he based justice on giving everyone his or her due.

chapters.title: Unit 2: The Strange Voyage of Sindbad

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Pre-reading — Prediction

  • Q: Q1. Look at the title and the pictures of the story and try to predict what happens in this voyage of Sindbad.
    Ans: Model prediction: From the title 'The Strange Voyage of Sindbad' and the pictures of a huge bird, a giant egg and an island, we can predict that Sindbad will sail to a strange island, be left alone there, meet a wonderful giant bird called a Roc and its huge egg, and escape from the island in an unusual and dangerous way after a wonderful adventure.

Glossary — Word Meanings (as printed in the book)

  • Q: What does 'dazzling' mean?
    Ans: Dazzling: so bright that you cannot see for a short time (as printed in the glossary).
  • Q: What does 'descending' mean?
    Ans: Descending: to come or go down from a higher to a lower level.
  • Q: What does 'immense' mean?
    Ans: Immense: extremely large or great.
  • Q: What does 'marvelous' mean?
    Ans: Marvelous: extremely good; wonderful. (Printed in the book as 'marvelous' in the glossary and 'marvelously' in the lesson.)
  • Q: What does 'amazement' mean?
    Ans: Amazement: a feeling of great surprise.
  • Q: What does 'hovering' mean?
    Ans: Hovering: to stay in the air in one place.
  • Q: What does 'swiftly' mean?
    Ans: Swiftly: quickly; after a very short time.
  • Q: What does 'desolate' mean?
    Ans: Desolate: empty and without people, making you feel sad or frightened. (In the lesson the same sense is used in 'the deserted island'.)
  • Q: What does 'inherited' mean?
    Ans: Inherited: to receive money, property, etc. from somebody when that person dies. Note: the right edge of this glossary line is cut off by a fold in the scanned page; the meaning is completed here from the visible words and standard dictionary wording.
  • Q: What does 'embarked' mean?
    Ans: Embarked: to get onto a ship; to put something onto a ship. Note: the right edge of this glossary line is cut off by a fold in the scanned page; the meaning is completed here from the visible words and standard dictionary wording.
  • Q: What does 'bargain' mean?
    Ans: Bargain: a thing bought for less than the usual price.
  • Q: What does 'perceive' mean?
    Ans: Perceive: to notice or become aware of something.
  • Q: What does 'despair' mean?
    Ans: Despair: the feeling of having lost all hope.
  • Q: What does 'curiosity' mean?
    Ans: Curiosity: a strong desire to know about something.
  • Q: What does 'turban' mean?
    Ans: Turban: a long piece of cloth wound tightly around the head.
  • Q: What does 'puzzled' mean?
    Ans: Puzzled: unable to understand something or the reason for something.
  • Q: What does 'securely' mean?
    Ans: Securely: in a way that is safe or protected against harm, crime, etc.

Comprehension A — Answer the Following Questions

  • Q: Q1. Write the character sketch of Sindbad.
    Ans: Sindbad is a brave, adventurous and resourceful sailor. He inherited considerable wealth from his parents but wasted it carelessly in his youth. When little was left, he became wise, sold his household goods and joined merchants who traded by sea. He is courageous: when he was left alone on the island he did not lose heart but took courage and looked for means of escape. He is clever and quick-thinking: he tied himself to the Roc's foot with his turban and later tied a piece of meat to his back so that an eagle carried him out of the valley of diamonds. He is also generous, because on reaching home his first action was to bestow large sums of money upon the poor.
  • Q: Q2. Why did Sindbad auction all his household goods?
    Ans: Sindbad had inherited considerable wealth from his parents, but being young and foolish he wasted it carelessly. Finding that riches speedily take to themselves wings if managed badly, he began to think how he could make the best of what still remained to him. So he sold all his household goods by public auction and, with the money, obtained goods suitable for the places he intended to visit and joined a company of merchants who traded by sea.
  • Q: Q3. Why did he spend night in a little cave?
    Ans: The Roc had carried Sindbad to a deep and narrow valley surrounded by steep, rocky mountains, and the ground of the valley was covered with diamonds. The valley was also full of horrible snakes so long and large that the smallest of them could have swallowed an elephant. Fortunately the snakes hid in the caves of the rocks by day, because of their enemy the Roc, and came out only by night. So, to save himself from the serpents, Sindbad crept into a little cave at dusk, blocked up the entrance with a stone, ate part of his food and spent the night there while the serpents crawled to and fro, hissing horribly outside.
  • Q: Q4. Identify the speaker or narrator of the story 'The Strange Voyage of Sindbad'.
    Ans: The speaker or narrator of the story is Sindbad himself. The story is told in the first person, as Sindbad narrates his own voyage: 'I had inherited considerable wealth from my parents', 'I sold all my household goods', 'I fell asleep', and so on throughout the story.
  • Q: Q5. What is the theme and setting of the story?
    Ans: Theme: The theme of the story is that courage, wisdom and presence of mind can save a person from the greatest dangers, and that riches are soon lost if they are managed badly but can be regained by hard work and cleverness. Setting: The story is set in the seas east of Africa and south of Asia, on a deserted island with springs of excellent water and fruit trees, and in a deep, narrow valley of diamonds surrounded by steep mountains that towered into the clouds.
  • Q: Q6. Who threw the large pieces of raw meat on the diamonds? Why?
    Ans: The merchants threw the large pieces of raw meat on the diamonds. They threw great lumps of meat into the valley from over the cliffs so that the diamonds stuck to the meat with force. When the eagles pounced upon the meat and carried it off to their nests to feed their hungry children, the merchants would scare the eagles away and secure the treasure (the diamonds) from the nests, because no man could climb down into the deep valley himself.
  • Q: Q7. Pick out at least three transitional devices from the text.
    Ans: Three transitional devices used in the text are: 'until one day' (We went from island to island... until one day we landed at a spot...), 'By this time' (By this time the sun was near setting...), and 'At last' (At last, I sat down upon a rock... / At last I reached home...). Other examples in the text are 'As soon as' (As soon as the dawn appeared the bird rose into the air...) and 'Before we left' (Before we left I exchanged one of my diamonds...).
  • Q: Q8. Suggest a new ending for the story.
    Ans: Suggested new ending: Sindbad could have shared his plan with the merchants before tying the meat to his back and asked them to wait near the eagles' nests. When the eagle dropped him into its nest, the merchants would rescue him at once, and in return Sindbad would divide his diamonds equally among them. The merchants, pleased with his honesty, would make him their partner, and together they would return home rich. Sindbad would then build a school for poor children with part of his wealth and live peacefully, always remembering that wisdom is greater than wealth.

Comprehension B — Choose the Correct Option

  • Q: Q1. The sky went dark because _____.
    Options: a big egg was lying there / a giant bird flew over Sindbad's head / merchants were throwing meat / it was about to rain heavily
    Ans: a giant bird flew over Sindbad's head
  • Q: Q2. Sindbad got money from the voyage by _____.
    Options: selling all his provisions / robbing the ship of the merchants / taking diamonds from the valley / finding money in the eagle's nest
    Ans: taking diamonds from the valley
  • Q: Q3. 'Riches speedily take to themselves wings if managed badly' means _____.
    Options: money goes very quickly if you are not careful / a rich man is like a bird with wings, it can fly away / working hard your whole life to be rich wastes your life / riches bring arrogance and pride that deceive men
    Ans: money goes very quickly if you are not careful
  • Q: Q4. Sindbad was left alone because _____.
    Options: the merchants were angry with him and refused to take him along / a giant bird took him into his nest / he saw diamonds in the valley and got greedy / he went to sleep on the island and his ship went away
    Ans: he went to sleep on the island and his ship went away
  • Q: Q5. Roc was an / a _____.
    Options: enormous legendary bird / huge mythical snake / gigantic egg of a bird / massive sized diamond
    Ans: enormous legendary bird

mcqs.q: The sky went dark because _____.
options: a big egg was lying there
a giant bird flew over Sindbad's head
it was about to rain heavily
mcqs.why: This is the book's own printed question, and its keyed answer is that a giant bird, the Roc, flew over Sindbad's head and darkened the sky.

mcqs.q: Sindbad got money from the voyage by _____.
options: robbing the ship of the merchants
finding money in the eagle's nest
mcqs.why: This is the book's own printed question, and its keyed answer is that Sindbad got money by taking diamonds from the valley, which he later exchanged and enjoyed at home.

mcqs.q: 'Riches speedily take to themselves wings if managed badly' means _____.
options: money goes very quickly if you are not careful
a rich man is like a bird with wings, it can fly away
working hard your whole life to be rich wastes your life
riches bring arrogance and pride that deceive men
mcqs.why: This is the book's own printed question, and its keyed answer is that money goes very quickly if you are not careful, which is what happened to Sindbad's inherited wealth.

mcqs.q: Sindbad was left alone because _____.
options: the merchants were angry with him and refused to take him along
a giant bird took him into his nest
he saw diamonds in the valley and got greedy
he went to sleep on the island and his ship went away
mcqs.why: This is the book's own printed question, and its keyed answer is that he went to sleep on the island and his ship went away, leaving him alone.

mcqs.q: Roc was an / a _____.
mcqs.why: This is the book's own printed question, and its keyed answer is that the Roc was an enormous legendary bird, whose egg Sindbad found on the island.

mcqs.q: Why did Sindbad auction all his household goods?
options: He wanted to buy a bigger house
He had wasted his inherited wealth carelessly and wanted to make the best of what remained
The merchants forced him to sell them
He wished to settle in another country
mcqs.why: The notes say Sindbad wasted the considerable wealth he inherited from his parents, so he sold all his household goods by public auction and joined merchants who traded by sea.

mcqs.q: Why did Sindbad spend the night in a little cave in the valley?
options: To hide his diamonds from the merchants
To watch the Roc from a safe place
To save himself from the serpents that came out at night
To wait for the merchants to return
mcqs.why: The notes say the valley's huge snakes hid in caves by day because of their enemy the Roc and came out only by night, so Sindbad blocked a little cave's entrance with a stone and slept there safely.

mcqs.q: Who is the speaker or narrator of the story 'The Strange Voyage of Sindbad'?
options: Sindbad himself, telling the story in the first person
mcqs.why: The notes identify the narrator as Sindbad himself, because the story is told in the first person: 'I had inherited considerable wealth from my parents', 'I sold all my household goods', and so on.

mcqs.q: What is the theme of the story?
options: Courage, wisdom and presence of mind can save a person from the greatest dangers
Wealth once lost can never be regained
Sea voyages always end in disaster
Diamonds are more valuable than wisdom
mcqs.why: The notes state the theme: courage, wisdom and presence of mind can save a person from the greatest dangers, and riches managed badly are soon lost but can be regained by hard work and cleverness.

mcqs.q: Why did the merchants throw large pieces of raw meat into the valley?
options: To feed the hungry snakes of the valley
So that diamonds would stick to the meat and eagles would carry it to their nests
To frighten the Roc away from its egg
To mark the path down into the valley
mcqs.why: The notes say the merchants threw meat into the valley so the diamonds stuck to it with force; eagles then carried the meat to their nests, where the merchants scared them away and secured the treasure.

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary A — Dictionary Meanings, Guide Words and Entry Words

  • Q: Q1. 'steep' — dictionary meaning, guide words and entry word.
    Ans: Steep means rising or falling sharply, almost upright, as the sides of the valley in the story. Entry word: steep. The guide words are the first and last entry words printed at the top of the dictionary page on which 'steep' appears; they differ from dictionary to dictionary, so they must be copied from the dictionary used in class.
  • Q: Q2. 'merchant' — dictionary meaning, guide words and entry word.
    Ans: Merchant means a person who buys and sells goods, especially in large amounts, as the merchants in the story who traded by sea. Entry word: merchant. The guide words are the first and last entry words at the top of its dictionary page and must be taken from the dictionary used in class.
  • Q: Q3. 'treasure' — dictionary meaning, guide words and entry word.
    Ans: Treasure means a collection of valuable things such as gold, silver and jewels, as the diamonds the merchants secured from the eagles' nests. Entry word: treasure. The guide words are the first and last entry words at the top of its dictionary page and must be taken from the dictionary used in class.
  • Q: Q4. 'scaring' — dictionary meaning, guide words and entry word.
    Ans: Scaring means frightening someone or making someone feel afraid, as the merchants scared the eagles away from their nests. Entry word: scare (the word is given in the -ing form 'scaring'). The guide words are the first and last entry words at the top of its dictionary page and must be taken from the dictionary used in class.
  • Q: Q5. 'bestow' — dictionary meaning, guide words and entry word.
    Ans: Bestow means to give something as an honour or gift, as Sindbad bestowed large sums of money upon the poor. Entry word: bestow. The guide words are the first and last entry words at the top of its dictionary page and must be taken from the dictionary used in class.
  • Q: Q6. 'kicking' — dictionary meaning, guide words and entry word.
    Ans: Kicking means hitting something or someone with the foot, as Sindbad kicked the diamonds out of his path in the valley. Entry word: kick (the word is given in the -ing form 'kicking'). The guide words are the first and last entry words at the top of its dictionary page and must be taken from the dictionary used in class.
  • Q: Q7. 'cliffs' — dictionary meaning, guide words and entry word.
    Ans: Cliffs means steep, high faces of rock, especially at the edge of the sea or, in the story, above the valley of diamonds from which the merchants threw the meat. Entry word: cliff (the word is given in the plural form 'cliffs'). The guide words are the first and last entry words at the top of its dictionary page and must be taken from the dictionary used in class.

Vocabulary B — Sentences in Sequential Order and Summary of the Story

  • Q: Q1. Put the given sentences in sequential order.
    Ans: The correct sequential order is: (1) I sold all my household goods by public auction and joined a company of merchants who traded by sea. (2) I ran here and there in despair, and found that the ship I sailed in has left the shore. (3) Taking off my turban I tied myself securely to it with the hope that the Roc, when it took flight next morning, would bear me away with it from the deserted island. (4) In the morning when the snakes went to their dens, I came tremblingly out of my cave and wandered up and down the valley. (5) I then chose the piece of meat which seemed most suited to my purpose and, with the aid of my turban, bound it firmly to my back. (6) I soon heard the flapping of their mighty wings above me and had the satisfaction of feeling one of them seize upon my piece of meat, and me with it, and rise slowly towards his nest. (7) The merchants agreed to take me along, I stayed with them several days, and then as they were journeying homewards, I gladly accompanied them.
  • Q: Q2. Summarize the story in sequential order.
    Ans: Summary of the story: Sindbad wasted the wealth he had inherited, so he sold his household goods, bought goods for trade and sailed with some merchants. On a deserted island he fell asleep and the ship left without him. He found a huge white object, which was the egg of a giant bird, the Roc. He tied himself to the Roc's foot with his turban, and the bird carried him to a deep valley covered with diamonds and full of giant snakes. He spent the night safely in a small cave. Next day he saw merchants throw lumps of meat into the valley; the diamonds stuck to the meat and eagles carried the meat to their nests. Sindbad filled his bag with the largest diamonds, tied a piece of meat to his back, and an eagle carried him up to its nest. The merchants rescued him, he shared his story and some diamonds with them, travelled home with them, gave large sums to the poor and settled down to enjoy his riches.

Grammar A — Common, Proper, Collective and Abstract Nouns

  • Q: Q1. Point out the nouns and say whether they are common, proper, collective or abstract: 'The book was lying on the table.'
    Ans: Nouns: book — common noun; table — common noun.
  • Q: Q2. Point out the nouns and say whether they are common, proper, collective or abstract: 'We cannot live without water.'
    Ans: Nouns: water — material noun (a common, uncountable noun). There is no proper, collective or abstract noun in this sentence.
  • Q: Q3. Point out the nouns and say whether they are common, proper, collective or abstract: 'He gave me a bunch of grapes.'
    Ans: Nouns: bunch — collective noun; grapes — common noun.
  • Q: Q4. Point out the nouns and say whether they are common, proper, collective or abstract: 'The jury has given its verdict.'
    Ans: Nouns: jury — collective noun; verdict — abstract noun.
  • Q: Q5. Point out the nouns and say whether they are common, proper, collective or abstract: 'Smoking is injurious to health.'
    Ans: Nouns: smoking — abstract noun; health — abstract noun.

Grammar B — Countable (C) and Uncountable (U) Nouns

  • Q: Q1. Decide whether the noun in bold is countable (C) or uncountable (U): 'My father drinks two big glasses of water every morning.'
    Ans: Glasses is countable (C). We can count glasses: one glass, two glasses.
  • Q: Q2. Decide whether the noun in bold is countable (C) or uncountable (U): 'The bread my mother prepares is delicious.'
    Ans: Bread is uncountable (U). We do not count bread as one bread, two breads; we say a loaf of bread.
  • Q: Q3. Decide whether the noun in bold is countable (C) or uncountable (U): 'Drivers must be careful; the road is slippery.'
    Ans: Drivers is countable (C). We can count drivers: one driver, many drivers.
  • Q: Q4. Decide whether the noun in bold is countable (C) or uncountable (U): 'Some policemen are organizing road traffic to avoid any accidents.'
    Ans: Policemen is countable (C). We can count policemen: one policeman, two policemen.
  • Q: Q5. Decide whether the noun in bold is countable (C) or uncountable (U): 'I bought three bottles of mineral water for our picnic.'
    Ans: Water is uncountable (U). We do not count water itself; we count bottles of water.

Grammar C — Write the Plural of the Following Words

  • Q: Q1. Write the plural of 'city'.
    Ans: Cities.
  • Q: Q2. Write the plural of 'house'.
    Ans: Houses.
  • Q: Q3. Write the plural of 'analysis'.
    Ans: Analyses.
  • Q: Q4. Write the plural of 'family'.
    Ans: Families.
  • Q: Q5. Write the plural of 'life'.
    Ans: Lives.
  • Q: Q6. Write the plural of 'photo'.
    Ans: Photos.
  • Q: Q7. Write the plural of 'phone'.
    Ans: Phones.
  • Q: Q8. Write the plural of 'sandwich'.
    Ans: Sandwiches.
  • Q: Q9. Write the plural of 'nurse'.
    Ans: Nurses.
  • Q: Q10. Write the plural of 'woman'.
    Ans: Women.
  • Q: Q11. Write the plural of 'elf'.
    Ans: Elves.
  • Q: Q12. Write the plural of 'cherry'.
    Ans: Cherries.
  • Q: Q13. Write the plural of 'tomato'.
    Ans: Tomatoes.
  • Q: Q14. Write the plural of 'hero'.
    Ans: Heroes.
  • Q: Q15. Write the plural of 'box'.
    Ans: Boxes.
  • Q: Q16. Write the plural of 'mosquito'.
    Ans: Mosquitoes.
  • Q: Q17. Write the plural of 'party'.
    Ans: Parties.
  • Q: Q18. Write the plural of 'system'.
    Ans: Systems.
  • Q: Q19. Write the plural of 'foot'.
    Ans: Feet.
  • Q: Q20. Write the plural of 'village'.
    Ans: Villages.
  • Q: Q21. Write the plural of 'fish'.
    Ans: Fish (the plural of fish is also 'fish').

Grammar D — Singular and Plural Forms Used in Sentences

  • Q: Q1. Use the singular and plural forms in sentences: 'manner — manners'.
    Ans: Manner (a way in which a thing is done): He solved the problem in a clever manner. Manners (polite social behaviour): We should teach good manners to children.
  • Q: Q2. Use the singular and plural forms in sentences: 'air — airs'.
    Ans: Air (atmosphere): Fresh air is necessary for good health. Airs (affected manners, pride): She gives herself airs after winning a small prize.
  • Q: Q3. Use the singular and plural forms in sentences: 'character — characters'.
    Ans: Character (the mental and moral qualities of a person): Sindbad was a man of brave character. Characters (people in a novel, play or film): The characters of 'The Arabian Nights' are famous all over the world.
  • Q: Q4. Use the singular and plural forms in sentences: 'blind — blinds'.
    Ans: Blind (unable to see): The kind man helped the blind man cross the road. Blinds (screens for windows): Please pull down the blinds because the sun is very strong.

mcqs.q: What does the dictionary word 'steep' mean, as used for the valley in the story?
options: Rising or falling sharply, almost upright
mcqs.why: The notes define 'steep' as rising or falling sharply, almost upright, like the sides of the valley of diamonds in the story.

mcqs.q: What is the entry word for 'scaring' in a dictionary?
options: Scaring itself, as a separate headword
mcqs.why: The notes explain that the entry word for 'scaring' is 'scare', because the word is given in its -ing form and dictionaries list it under the base form.

mcqs.q: What is the entry word for 'cliffs' in a dictionary?
options: Cliffs itself, as a separate headword
mcqs.why: The notes explain that the entry word for 'cliffs' is 'cliff', because the word is given in its plural form and dictionaries list it under the singular form.

mcqs.q: What does the word 'bestow' mean, as in Sindbad bestowing money upon the poor?
options: To give something as an honour or gift
mcqs.why: The notes define 'bestow' as to give something as an honour or gift, as Sindbad bestowed large sums of money upon the poor on reaching home.

mcqs.q: What does the word 'treasure' mean in the story?
options: A collection of valuable things such as gold, silver and jewels
A large bird that lives near the sea
A piece of raw meat thrown by merchants
A bag used for carrying provisions
mcqs.why: The notes define 'treasure' as a collection of valuable things such as gold, silver and jewels, like the diamonds the merchants secured from the eagles' nests.

mcqs.q: In the sentence 'The book was lying on the table', the nouns 'book' and 'table' are:
mcqs.why: The notes classify both 'book' and 'table' in this sentence as common nouns, because they name ordinary things rather than particular persons or places.

mcqs.q: In the sentence 'The jury has given its verdict', 'jury' is a collective noun and 'verdict' is:
mcqs.why: The notes classify 'jury' as a collective noun and 'verdict' as an abstract noun, because a verdict is an idea or judgement, not a thing that can be touched.

mcqs.q: In the sentence 'He gave me a bunch of grapes', the word 'bunch' is:
mcqs.why: The notes classify 'bunch' in this sentence as a collective noun, because it names a group of grapes taken together, while 'grapes' is a common noun.

mcqs.q: In 'My father drinks two big glasses of water every morning', the noun 'glasses' is:
options: Uncountable, because water cannot be counted
Countable, because we can count one glass, two glasses
Abstract, because it names an idea
Proper, because it names a person
mcqs.why: The notes mark 'glasses' as countable (C) because we can count glasses: one glass, two glasses, even though the water inside them is uncountable.

mcqs.q: The noun 'bread' in 'The bread my mother prepares is delicious' is:
options: Countable, as in one bread, two breads
Uncountable, because we say a loaf of bread
mcqs.why: The notes mark 'bread' as uncountable (U) because we do not count bread as one bread, two breads; instead we say a loaf of bread.

mcqs.q: In 'I bought three bottles of mineral water for our picnic', the noun 'water' is:
options: Countable, because there are three bottles
Uncountable, because we count bottles of water, not water itself
mcqs.why: The notes mark 'water' as uncountable (U) in this sentence because we do not count water itself; we count the bottles of water.

mcqs.q: What is the plural of 'city'?
mcqs.why: The notes give the plural of 'city' as 'cities', because a noun ending in a consonant plus 'y' changes the 'y' to 'i' and adds 'es'.

mcqs.q: What is the plural of 'analysis'?
mcqs.why: The notes give the plural of 'analysis' as 'analyses', one of the irregular plural forms listed in the plural exercise.

mcqs.q: What is the plural of 'life'?
mcqs.why: The notes give the plural of 'life' as 'lives', because nouns ending in 'f' or 'fe' often change to 'ves' in the plural, like 'elf' becoming 'elves'.

mcqs.q: What is the plural of 'fish'?
options: Fish — the plural is the same as the singular
mcqs.why: The notes state clearly that the plural of 'fish' is also 'fish', so the singular and plural forms of this noun are the same.

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Writing

  • Q: QA. Write the story 'The Strange Voyage of Sindbad' in your own words in the third person (in sequential order, using specific adjectives and adverbs, appropriate tense and transitional devices, and the thoughts and emotions of the participants).
    Ans: The Strange Voyage of Sindbad (in third person): Sindbad inherited considerable wealth from his parents, but he wasted it carelessly in his youth. When little remained, he sold all his household goods by public auction, bought suitable goods and embarked in a good ship with other merchants. They went from island to island, making excellent bargains, until one day they landed on a beautiful island with springs of excellent water. While his companions wandered about, Sindbad ate his provisions in a shady place and fell asleep. When he woke up, he found with horror that he was alone and the ship was gone. He climbed a tall tree, and landwards he saw a huge, dazzling white object. Going near, he found it was a smooth white ball of immense size — the egg of a wonderful bird called a Roc. When the Roc settled on its egg, Sindbad tied himself with his turban to one of its feet, which was as large as the trunk of a tree. Next morning the bird carried him high into the air and then descended into a deep, narrow valley. He untied himself and found the ground covered with diamonds, but also full of horrible snakes that could swallow an elephant. At dusk he crept into a little cave, blocked its entrance with a stone and spent the night safely. The next day, huge pieces of fresh meat fell into the valley: the merchants above threw them so that diamonds stuck to them, and eagles carried the meat to their nests. Sindbad filled his provision bag with the largest diamonds, tied it to his belt, bound a big piece of meat firmly to his back and lay down. Soon an eagle seized the meat and carried him up to its nest. The merchants, who were watching, scared the eagle away and were amazed to find Sindbad. He told them his story and showed them his diamonds. They agreed to take him along, and after exchanging one diamond for goodly merchandise on the way, he reached home. His first action was to bestow large sums of money upon the poor, after which he settled down to enjoy the riches he had gained with so much toil and pain.
  • Q: QB. Write a paragraph of about 150 words describing the dangerous situation you had during an adventurous journey, using appropriate pronoun-antecedent relationship and transitional devices within the paragraph.
    Ans: Last winter, my friends and I set out to climb a high, rocky hill near our village. At first, the weather was pleasant and we climbed happily, but suddenly dark clouds covered the sky and a strong wind began to blow. Then heavy rain made the narrow path slippery and dangerous. One of my friends slipped and hurt his knee; he could not walk properly. We were frightened because the river below was rising fast and night was coming near. However, we did not lose courage. We tied our scarves together, made a strong support for our injured friend and helped him climb down slowly, step by step. Meanwhile, two of us went ahead to call the elders of the village. Finally, they reached us with ropes and torches and brought us home safely. That dangerous journey taught me that courage and teamwork can save us in the hardest situations.

mcqs.q: In the third-person version of the story, how did Sindbad lose his wealth at the start?
options: Pirates robbed his ship at sea
He wasted the considerable wealth he inherited, carelessly, in his youth
The merchants cheated him in trade
A flood destroyed his house and goods
mcqs.why: The third-person retelling in the notes begins by saying Sindbad inherited considerable wealth from his parents but wasted it carelessly in his youth, until little remained.

mcqs.q: After selling his household goods, what did Sindbad do, according to the retelling?
options: He built a shop in his own city
He bought suitable goods and embarked in a good ship with other merchants
He returned to his parents' house
He settled on the deserted island
mcqs.why: The retelling in the notes says he sold his goods by public auction, bought suitable goods and embarked in a good ship with other merchants, going from island to island.

mcqs.q: Where did Sindbad fall asleep on the island, according to the retelling?
options: Inside a little cave in the valley
On the deck of the ship
In a shady place, after eating his provisions
mcqs.why: The retelling in the notes says that while his companions wandered about, Sindbad ate his provisions in a shady place and fell asleep, and woke to find the ship gone.

mcqs.q: What was the huge, dazzling white object that Sindbad saw on the island?
options: The egg of a wonderful bird called a Roc
mcqs.why: The retelling in the notes says the huge white object was a smooth white ball of immense size — the egg of a wonderful bird called a Roc.

mcqs.q: How large was one foot of the Roc, according to the retelling?
options: As large as a ship's mast
As large as a man's arm
As large as the trunk of a tree
mcqs.why: The retelling in the notes says Sindbad tied himself to one of the Roc's feet, which was as large as the trunk of a tree.

mcqs.q: What danger, besides the snakes, is described about the valley in the retelling?
options: The ground was covered with diamonds, but the snakes there could swallow an elephant
The valley was flooded with deep water
The Roc nested in the valley every night
mcqs.why: The retelling in the notes says he found the ground covered with diamonds, but also full of horrible snakes so large that they could have swallowed an elephant.

mcqs.q: How did Sindbad protect himself in the cave at dusk, according to the retelling?
options: He lit a large fire at the entrance
He blocked the cave's entrance with a stone
He climbed a tall tree instead
He hid under a piece of meat
mcqs.why: The retelling in the notes says that at dusk he crept into a little cave, blocked its entrance with a stone and spent the night safely while the serpents moved outside.

mcqs.q: What did Sindbad do with the largest diamonds, according to the retelling?
options: He threw them back into the valley
He gave them all to the merchants
He filled his provision bag with them and tied it to his belt
He hid them inside the cave
mcqs.why: The retelling in the notes says Sindbad filled his provision bag with the largest diamonds and tied it to his belt before binding a big piece of meat to his back.

mcqs.q: What was Sindbad's first action on reaching home, according to the retelling?
options: He bought a new ship at once
He bestowed large sums of money upon the poor
He built a palace for himself
mcqs.why: The retelling in the notes says his first action on reaching home was to bestow large sums of money upon the poor, after which he settled down to enjoy his riches.

mcqs.q: In the model paragraph about a dangerous journey, what lesson did the writer learn?
options: Mountains should never be climbed in winter
Heavy rain always stops a journey
Courage and teamwork can save us in the hardest situations
Travelling alone is safer than travelling in a group
mcqs.why: The model paragraph in the notes ends by saying that the dangerous journey taught the writer that courage and teamwork can save us in the hardest situations.

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Pre-reading

  • Q: Q1. Why do people sometimes build cities or towns near a river?
    Ans: People build cities or towns near a river because a river provides water for drinking, farming and daily use, fertile land for crops, and an easy route for travel and trade. The lesson also warns that living too close to rivers and ravines is risky, because such settlements can be flooded and destroyed when the river overflows.
  • Q: Q2. What are different disasters?
    Ans: Different disasters include floods, earthquakes, fires, explosions, toxic chemical spillages, droughts and storms. Some disasters are natural, such as floods and earthquakes, while others are man-made, such as wars, terrorism, fires and industrial accidents. A disaster happens when a hazard harms people who are vulnerable to it.

Glossary — Word Meanings

  • Q: What does 'unfettered' mean?
    Ans: Not controlled or restricted.
  • Q: What does 'chopped' mean?
    Ans: To cut something into pieces with a sharp tool such as a knife.
  • Q: What does 'catastrophic' mean?
    Ans: Causing a lot of damage and suffering.
  • Q: What does 'rendered' mean?
    Ans: To cause somebody or something to be in a particular state or condition.
  • Q: What does 'malnutrition' mean?
    Ans: A poor condition of health caused by a lack of food or a lack of the right type of food.
  • Q: What does 'embankments' mean?
    Ans: A wall of stone or earth made to keep water back or to carry a road or railway/railroad over low ground.
  • Q: What does 'channelize' mean?
    Ans: As printed in the glossary: a passage that water can flow along, especially in the ground, on the bottom of a river, etc. In the lesson it is used for making channels to direct floodwater away.
  • Q: What does 'imminent' mean?
    Ans: Likely to happen very soon.
  • Q: What does 'phenomenon' mean?
    Ans: A fact or an event in nature or society, especially one that is not fully understood.
  • Q: What does 'vulnerable' mean?
    Ans: Weak and easily hurt physically or emotionally.
  • Q: What does 'settlements' mean?
    Ans: As printed in the glossary: an official agreement that ends an argument between two people or groups. In the lesson, the word is used for places where people live, such as villages and towns near rivers.
  • Q: What does 'cope' mean?
    Ans: To deal successfully with something difficult.
  • Q: What does 'ravine' mean?
    Ans: A deep, very narrow valley with steep sides.
  • Q: What does 'livestock' mean?
    Ans: The animals kept on a farm, for example cows or sheep.
  • Q: What does 'mitigated' mean?
    Ans: To make something less harmful, serious, etc.
  • Q: What does 'evacuation' mean?
    Ans: The process of moving people from a place of danger to a safer place.

Comprehension A — Answer the following questions

  • Q: Q1. How did the floods of 2010 affect the people and environment?
    Ans: The floods of 2010 were one of the worst disasters in the history of Pakistan. They affected approximately 20 million people and claimed about 2,000 lives. The flood destroyed homes, crops and infrastructure, and approximately 1.6 million people were rendered homeless. Millions of people became vulnerable to malnutrition and waterborne diseases.
  • Q: Q2. How would you differentiate between a hazard and a disaster?
    Ans: A hazard is a phenomenon or process, either natural or man-made, that can endanger a group of people, their belongings and their environment if they do not take precautions. A hazard converts into a disaster when it actually harms people who are vulnerable to it. For example, a river is a hazard for people living too close to it, and it becomes a disaster when it floods and destroys their settlements.
  • Q: Q3. What is meant by vulnerability to disasters?
    Ans: Vulnerability to disasters means being weak and easily harmed by a hazard. People who have no preparation and no training, and who do not know how to deal with the situation, are more vulnerable than those who can cope with the hazard. When a hazard like an earthquake or flood strikes, such unprepared people are the worst hit.
  • Q: Q4. How can we mitigate the risks of floods?
    Ans: We can mitigate the risks of floods by planning and preparing before the disaster strikes. People should be warned about an imminent flood through announcements on loudspeakers and helped to move to safe places. Livestock and valuable household items should be shifted to safe places, clean water should be arranged for the affected people, housing should be planned at safe locations, mud walls and rooftops should be repaired before the rainy season, river embankments should be properly secured, and drains should be dug to channelize floodwater.
  • Q: Q5. What measures should the schools take for minimizing the risks of floods?
    Ans: All schools should have School Safety Plans, including easy to execute evacuation plans. Schools should ensure that students follow the instructions provided through periodic drills for disaster preparedness. The attendance registers should always be updated to know the exact head count, so that it can be ensured that all students present are evacuated safely.
  • Q: Q6. What steps can the government take to lessen the risks of disaster?
    Ans: The government should work closely with the communities and synchronize all efforts to reduce the risks of disaster. Besides providing timely information on the imminent hazards, it should also ensure that all risks are mitigated to reduce the dangerous effects of floods.
  • Q: Q7. What factors contribute to floods?
    Ans: Floods occur when heavy rainfall leads to the unfettered flow of large quantities of water that the soil is unable to absorb. Monsoon rains were the chief cause of the devastating floods of 2010. The soil also loses its ability to absorb water particularly in areas where people have chopped down trees without planting new ones, which further contributes to floods.
  • Q: Q8. Identify at least one sentence having an opinion and a sentence indicating fact.
    Ans: Sentence indicating fact: 'The flood usurped homes, crops, and infrastructure, and claimed about 2,000 lives.' This is a fact because it states what actually happened and can be verified. Sentence having an opinion: 'She declared 2010 floods to be one of the worst disasters in the history of Pakistan.' This is an opinion because calling the floods 'one of the worst' is the teacher's judgement and evaluation of the event.

Comprehension B — Use summary skill to complete the cloze paragraph

  • Q: The teacher further added _____ Natural Hazards can be catastrophic for the communities that fall victim to them.
    Ans: that
  • Q: The teacher further added that Natural Hazards can be _____ for the communities that fall victim to them.
    Ans: catastrophic
  • Q: Natural Hazards can be catastrophic for the communities that _____ victim to them.
    Ans: fall
  • Q: In _____ reflective manner, she declared 2010 floods to be one of the worst disasters in the history of Pakistan.
    Ans: a
  • Q: In a reflective manner, she declared _____ floods to be one of the worst disasters in the history of Pakistan.
    Ans: 2010
  • Q: She declared 2010 floods to be one _____ the worst disasters in the history of Pakistan.
    Ans: of
  • Q: 2010 floods were one of the worst disasters in _____ history of Pakistan.
    Ans: the
  • Q: It was one of the worst disasters in the history of Pakistan for _____ affected approximately 20 million people.
    Ans: it
  • Q: The floods affected approximately 20 million _____.
    Ans: people
  • Q: The flood usurped homes, _____, and infrastructure, and claimed about 2,000 lives.
    Ans: crops
  • Q: The flood usurped homes, crops, and infrastructure, and claimed _____ 2,000 lives.
    Ans: about
  • Q: Millions of _____ people became vulnerable to malnutrition and waterborne diseases.
    Ans: the
  • Q: Millions of the people became vulnerable to _____ and waterborne diseases.
    Ans: malnutrition
  • Q: Millions became vulnerable to malnutrition and waterborne diseases and _____ 1.6 million people were rendered homeless.
    Ans: approximately
  • Q: Approximately 1.6 million people were _____ homeless.
    Ans: rendered

mcqs.q: Why do people sometimes build cities or towns near a river?
options: Because rivers provide water, fertile land, and an easy route for travel and trade
Because rivers keep wild animals away
Because land near rivers is always safe
Because rivers make the weather cooler only
mcqs.why: The notes say people build near a river because it provides water for drinking, farming and daily use, fertile land for crops, and an easy route for travel and trade.

mcqs.q: According to the notes, which of the following is a man-made disaster?
mcqs.why: The notes list floods, earthquakes and droughts as natural disasters, while wars, terrorism, fires and industrial accidents are given as man-made disasters.

mcqs.q: Approximately how many people were affected by the floods of 2010 in Pakistan?
mcqs.why: The notes state that the floods of 2010 affected approximately 20 million people and claimed about 2,000 lives, making them one of the worst disasters in Pakistan's history.

mcqs.q: Approximately how many people were rendered homeless by the floods of 2010?
mcqs.why: The notes state that approximately 1.6 million people were rendered homeless by the 2010 floods, which also destroyed homes, crops and infrastructure.

mcqs.q: What is a hazard, according to the lesson?
options: A phenomenon or process that can endanger people, their belongings and their environment if they do not take precautions
A disaster that has already destroyed a city
A plan made by the government after a flood
A wall of earth built to keep water back
mcqs.why: The notes define a hazard as a phenomenon or process, natural or man-made, that can endanger a group of people, their belongings and their environment if they do not take precautions.

mcqs.q: When does a hazard convert into a disaster?
options: When people build houses far from a river
When it actually harms people who are vulnerable to it
When the government announces it on loudspeakers
When it rains heavily for one day
mcqs.why: The notes explain that a hazard converts into a disaster when it actually harms people who are vulnerable to it, as when a river floods and destroys the settlements near it.

mcqs.q: What is meant by vulnerability to disasters?
options: Being strong and fully prepared for danger
Being weak and easily harmed by a hazard, with no preparation or training
Living in a large city near a river
Knowing how to swim in floodwater
mcqs.why: The notes say vulnerability means being weak and easily harmed by a hazard; people with no preparation and no training are more vulnerable and are the worst hit when a hazard strikes.

mcqs.q: Which factor contributes to floods, according to the lesson?
options: Planting more trees on river banks
People chopping down trees without planting new ones, so the soil loses its ability to absorb water

options: By warning people through loudspeaker announcements and helping them move to safe places
By waiting until the water enters the houses
By cutting down trees near the river
By keeping livestock in low-lying areas

mcqs.q: Why should schools always keep their attendance registers updated?
options: To know the exact head count, so it can be ensured that all students present are evacuated safely
To award prizes to regular students
To inform parents about examination results
To plan the school timetable for the year
mcqs.why: The notes say attendance registers should always be updated to know the exact head count, so that it can be ensured that all students present are evacuated safely during a disaster.

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary — Utilize comparison clues to deduce the meaning of underlined words

  • Q: My best friend has been a companion to me for five years. In this sentence, the word 'companion' means:
    Options: mother / friend / brother / father
    Ans: friend
  • Q: I meandered through the woods and did not win the race. In this sentence, the word 'meandered' means:
    Options: jogged / ran / hurried / wandered
    Ans: wandered
  • Q: In the pirate story, there were the good guys against the buccaneers. In this sentence, the word 'buccaneers' means:
    Options: actors / helpers / students / pirates
    Ans: pirates
  • Q: If you don't conquer your fears, they will beat you. In this sentence, the word 'conquer' means:
    Options: talk about / lose / win / love
    Ans: win
  • Q: The good guy in the story was strong and kind, unlike the villain. In this sentence, the word 'villain' means:
    Options: superhero / friend / bad guy / hero
    Ans: bad guy

Grammar A — Change the gender in the following sentences

  • Q: Q1. Change the gender: She met that girl at the party.
    Ans: He met that boy at the party.
  • Q: Q2. Change the gender: This lady is rowing a boat.
    Ans: This man is rowing a boat.
  • Q: Q3. Change the gender: He told his teacher the truth.
    Ans: She told her teacher the truth.
  • Q: Q4. Change the gender: The cow ate the green grass.
    Ans: The ox ate the green grass.
  • Q: Q5. Change the gender: The hen is a useful bird.
    Ans: The cock is a useful bird.

Grammar B — Circle the correct possessive nouns, keeping in view animate and inanimate nouns

  • Q: Choose the correct possessive form: The desk's edge / edge of the desk is very sharp and pointed.
    Options: The desk's edge / edge of the desk
    Ans: edge of the desk
  • Q: Choose the correct possessive form: She plans on opening a men's / mens fashion apparel.
    Options: men's / mens
    Ans: men's
  • Q: Choose the correct possessive form: Children's / childrens' software development is not of high importance.
    Options: Children's / childrens'
    Ans: Children's
  • Q: Choose the correct possessive form: The sheep's food supply / food supply of the sheep was threatened.
    Options: The sheep's food supply / food supply of the sheep
    Ans: The sheep's food supply
  • Q: Choose the correct possessive form: The lions' / lions's usual source of water has dried up.
    Options: lions' / lions's
    Ans: lions'
  • Q: Choose the correct possessive form: The two mothers-in-law's cooking / mother-in-laws' cooking was awesome.
    Options: mothers-in-law's cooking / mother-in-laws' cooking
    Ans: mothers-in-law's cooking
  • Q: Choose the correct possessive form: The witches' brooms / brooms of the witches were hidden in the corner.
    Options: witches' brooms / brooms of the witches
    Ans: witches' brooms
  • Q: Choose the correct possessive form: The hotel's windows / windows of the hotel are beautifully constructed.
    Options: The hotel's windows / windows of the hotel
    Ans: windows of the hotel

mcqs.q: My best friend has been a companion to me for five years. In this sentence, the word 'companion' means:
mcqs.why: This is the book's own printed question, and its keyed answer is 'friend', because a companion is a friend who keeps you company, as the comparison clue 'best friend' shows.

mcqs.q: I meandered through the woods and did not win the race. In this sentence, the word 'meandered' means:
mcqs.why: This is the book's own printed question, and its keyed answer is 'wandered', because someone who wandered through the woods would not win a race.

mcqs.q: In the pirate story, there were the good guys against the buccaneers. In this sentence, the word 'buccaneers' means:
mcqs.why: This is the book's own printed question, and its keyed answer is 'pirates', because the comparison clue 'in the pirate story' shows that buccaneers are pirates.

mcqs.q: If you don't conquer your fears, they will beat you. In this sentence, the word 'conquer' means:
mcqs.why: This is the book's own printed question, and its keyed answer is 'win', because the opposite clue 'they will beat you' shows that to conquer is to win over something.

mcqs.q: The good guy in the story was strong and kind, unlike the villain. In this sentence, the word 'villain' means:
mcqs.why: This is the book's own printed question, and its keyed answer is 'bad guy', because the word 'unlike' contrasts the strong and kind good guy with the villain.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct possessive form: The _____ is very sharp and pointed. (the desk is an inanimate thing)
mcqs.why: This is the book's own printed item, and its keyed answer is 'edge of the desk', because for inanimate nouns the possessive is shown with 'of' rather than an apostrophe.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct possessive form: She plans on opening a _____ fashion apparel.
mcqs.why: This is the book's own printed item, and its keyed answer is 'men's', because 'men' is a plural noun that does not end in 's', so the possessive adds apostrophe plus 's'.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct possessive form: _____ software development is not of high importance.
mcqs.why: This is the book's own printed item, and its keyed answer is 'Children's', because 'children' is a plural noun that does not end in 's', so the possessive adds apostrophe plus 's'.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct possessive form: _____ was threatened. (the food supply belonging to the sheep)
mcqs.why: This is the book's own printed item, and its keyed answer is 'The sheep's food supply', because the sheep is an animate noun, so its possessive is formed with an apostrophe.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct possessive form for a group of lions: The _____ usual source of water has dried up.
mcqs.why: This is the book's own printed item, and its keyed answer is 'lions'', because 'lions' is a plural noun ending in 's', so only an apostrophe is added to show possession.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct possessive form: The two _____ cooking was awesome.
mcqs.why: This is the book's own printed item, and its keyed answer is 'mothers-in-law's cooking', because the plural of the compound noun is 'mothers-in-law' and the possessive is added at the end.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct possessive form: The _____ were hidden in the corner. (brooms belonging to the witches)
mcqs.why: This is the book's own printed item, and its keyed answer is 'witches' brooms', because 'witches' is a plural animate noun ending in 's', so only an apostrophe is added.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct possessive form: The _____ are beautifully constructed. (the hotel is an inanimate thing)
mcqs.why: This is the book's own printed item, and its keyed answer is 'windows of the hotel', because for inanimate nouns the possessive is shown with 'of' rather than an apostrophe.
