lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Writing A — Complete the mind map and write the summary of the lesson 'The Handicrafts of Pakistan'

  • Q: Complete the mind map of 'The Handicrafts of Pakistan'.
    Ans: Mind map branches around 'The Handicrafts of Pakistan': (1) Topi (cap) and Ajrak (shawl) of Sindh, with Rilli patchwork quilts of Sindh and Balochistan; (2) Blue pottery of Multan, Bahawalpur and Hala, and camel-skin lamps of Multan; (3) Brassware of Peshawar and wood carving of Chiniot and areas adjacent to Kashmir, inlaid with ivory; (4) Cane basket work, embroidery of Swat, D. G. Khan, Chitral and Balochistan; (5) Marble carving of Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and onyx show pieces; (6) Sports goods, surgical goods, tableware and bagpipes of Sialkot.
  • Q: Write the summary of the lesson 'The Handicrafts of Pakistan'.
    Ans: Pakistan is a land of colours and rich culture, with a heritage 7000-9000 years old, and every region has its own handicrafts. Multan, Bahawalpur and Hala are famous for paper-thin blue pottery, while brassware plates, vases and bowls remind us of the great Mughal period, and brass work is done in Peshawar on utensils and decoration pieces. Chiniot and the areas near Kashmir are famous for wood carving and woodcrafts inlaid with ivory, and the carved wooden furniture is exported in huge quantities. Skilled craftsmen weave cane into baskets, handbags and mats, and embroidery such as Swat thread work, D. G. Khan mirror work, Chitrali Patti and Kadhai, and Balochistan needle-work is sought after all over the world. Marble carving of Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa may go back to the Palaeolithic age, Sialkot makes world-famous sports goods, surgical goods and bagpipes, Multan makes camel-skin lamps, and Sindh is known for Rilli quilts, Topi and Ajrak. These handicrafts give jobs to a large number of people and depict the rich cultural heritage and glorious history of Pakistan.

Writing B — Analyse the first paragraph of the lesson: topic sentence, specific words, vivid verbs and modifiers

  • Q: Read the first paragraph of the lesson carefully. Underline (identify) the topic sentence, specific words, vivid verbs and modifiers.
    Ans: Topic sentence: 'Our beautiful country Pakistan is a land of colours and rich culture.' It tells the main idea of the whole paragraph, that Pakistan's rich culture shows itself in its handicrafts. Specific words: Pakistan, cultural heritage, handicrafts, tradition, culture, dialects, folklore, music, dresses and costumes. Vivid verbs: 'has inherited' and 'have left' (in 'The imprints left by successive civilizations have left a rich heritage of handicrafts'). Modifiers: beautiful (country), rich (culture, cultural heritage, heritage), successive (civilizations), different (regions) and wide (variety).

Writing C — Write a simple and unified paragraph on 'Handicrafts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa'

  • Q: After brainstorming and developing ideas, write a simple and unified paragraph on 'Handicrafts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa', with a clear topic sentence using specific words, vivid words and modifiers.
    Ans: Topic sentence: 'The skilled artisans of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa create beautiful handicrafts that proudly display the rich culture of the province.' In Peshawar, craftsmen hammer shining brass into useful household utensils and lovely decoration pieces. Patient carvers of the province cut hard marble into decorative articles and eye-catching onyx show pieces. In the northern areas and hill stations, craftsmen weave stripped cane into strong baskets, handbags and mats that tourists eagerly buy. Swat is well-known for its fine thread embroidery, while the colourful Chitrali Patti is woven on handlooms and neat Kadhai is done on the warm Chitrali Chugha. These handicrafts give work to many families and carry the name of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa all over the world.

lessons.notes_html:
Listening and Speaking — Express dissatisfaction, disapproval and disagreement politely

  • Q: In pairs develop and practise a dialogue to express your feelings of disaffection, disapproval and disagreement in daily life. Give a model dialogue.
    Ans: Model dialogue: A: 'I am sorry to say this, but I am not quite happy with the bag I bought from this shop yesterday. Its handle has already come loose.' B: 'I do apologise for that. Would you like me to replace it?' A: 'Yes, please, but I am afraid I do not agree with taking the same design again. It does not seem strong enough.' B: 'No problem at all. Please choose another design, and I will exchange it at once.' A: 'Thank you for understanding. I really appreciate your help.' The speakers express dissatisfaction, disapproval and disagreement politely by using soft expressions such as 'I am sorry to say', 'I am afraid' and 'I do not agree', instead of rude words.

chapters.title: Unit 8: Letter to the Editor of a Newspaper

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Pre-reading — Format for Formal Letter

  • Q: What comes first in the format of a formal letter?
    Ans: A formal letter begins with the sender's address at the top, for example 'abc Colony, ABC City-400005', followed by the date of writing the letter, for example 'Dated: 14 May 2017'.
  • Q: What is written after the date in a formal letter?
    Ans: After the sender's address and date, we write the receiver's designation and address, for example 'The Editor, XYZ Colony, XYZ City-400001', so that the letter reaches the right person.
  • Q: What is the subject of a formal letter?
    Ans: The subject is a short description, in one sentence, of the cause or purpose of writing the letter, for example the subject of the model letter in this unit is 'Awareness among the public about pollution hazards'.
  • Q: What salutation is used in a formal letter?
    Ans: The salutation is the polite greeting to the receiver, such as 'Respected Sir/Madam,' or 'Dear Sir/Madam,'. It is written after the subject and before the body of the letter.
  • Q: What are the three parts of the body of a formal letter?
    Ans: The body of the letter has three parts: (i) Introduction, in which the writer introduces himself and the purpose of writing; (ii) Main content, in which the matter is explained in detail; and (iii) Conclusion and end of the letter, in which the writer sums up and states what he hopes for.
  • Q: How does a formal letter end?
    Ans: A formal letter ends with a complimentary closing such as 'Thanking you, Yours sincerely / faithfully / truly,' followed by the name of the sender and the designation, if present.

Comprehension A — Answer the following questions

  • Q: Q1. Identify different kinds of pollution.
    Ans: The different kinds of pollution named in the letter are air pollution, water pollution, noise pollution and land (soil) pollution. Pollution is basically contamination, that is, making air, water or land dirty and harmful with unwanted substances.
  • Q: Q2. Explain why it is important to keep the environment free of pollution.
    Ans: It is important to keep the environment free of pollution because pollution harms human, plant and animal life and causes many diseases, such as cancer, cholera, typhoid and insomnia. A clean environment gives us clean air to breathe, safe water to drink and healthy soil for food, and people can fight pollution only when they are aware of its types and of the results of not controlling it.
  • Q: Q3. How does pollution affect our environment?
    Ans: Pollution affects our environment in many harmful ways. Air pollution causes global warming, acid rain and depletion of the ozone layer, so people are exposed to harmful UV rays. Water pollution destroys water life, disturbs the whole food chain and deprives people of drinking water. Land pollution spoils or even poisons our food through plants and contaminates groundwater, and noise pollution disturbs sleep, rest and health.
  • Q: Q4. What are some things we can do to prevent further pollution of our earth?
    Ans: To prevent further pollution we should become aware of its causes and effects and make others aware too. We should not dump waste recklessly into rivers, ponds and land, we should dispose of garbage through proper disposal systems, and we should reduce the excessive use of fertilizers and pesticides. We should also control smoke and noise from vehicles and industries, and play our role in making the environment clean, as the writer of the letter hopes.
  • Q: Q5. Find at least three causes of pollution and their effect on the environment from the letter.
    Ans: (1) Cars, motorized vehicles and industries release harmful contaminants into the air; this causes global warming, acid rain and ozone layer depletion, and increases lung cancer and skin cancer. (2) Industrial effluents and people recklessly dumping waste into ponds, lakes, rivers and oceans pollute water; this kills water life, affects the entire food chain and causes diarrhoeal diseases such as cholera, typhoid and dysentery. (3) Over dumping, over utilization of soil and excessive use of fertilizers and pesticides pollute the land; plants absorb the harmful chemicals, so food is spoiled or poisoned and groundwater becomes contaminated.

Comprehension B — Choose the correct option

  • Q: 1. Noise is _____
    Options: loud sound / unwanted sound / constant sound / slow sound
    Ans: unwanted sound
  • Q: 2. _____ causes air pollution.
    Options: ozone / oxygen / industries / pesticides
    Ans: industries
  • Q: 3. The diseases cholera, typhoid and jaundice are due to _____ pollution.
    Options: air / water / soil / food items
    Ans: water
  • Q: 4. All of the following are water hygiene diseases except _____.
    Options: insomnia / typhoid / dysentery / cholera
    Ans: insomnia
  • Q: 5. Land pollution is the _____
    Options: contamination of the air when harmful contaminants are released into the air / contamination of the soil that is caused due to over dumping / pollution caused mostly due to traffic and pressure horns / contamination of water bodies such as ponds, lakes, rivers, oceans
    Ans: contamination of the soil that is caused due to over dumping

Glossary — Word Meanings

  • Q: What does 'contaminated' mean?
    Ans: To make a substance or place dirty or no longer pure by adding a substance that is dangerous or carries disease.
  • Q: What does 'pesticides' mean?
    Ans: A chemical used for killing an insect or animal that destroys plants, food, etc.
  • Q: What does 'migraine' mean?
    Ans: Headache that is felt in one half of the head.
  • Q: What does 'fatigue' mean?
    Ans: A feeling of being extremely tired, usually because of hard work or exercise.
  • Q: What does 'delve into' mean?
    Ans: To try hard to find out more information about something.
  • Q: What does 'hazards' mean?
    Ans: A thing that can be dangerous or cause damage.
  • Q: What does 'repercussion' mean?
    Ans: An indirect and usually bad result of an action or event that may happen sometime afterwards.
  • Q: What does 'esteemed' mean?
    Ans: Great respect and admiration; a good opinion of somebody.
  • Q: What does 'awareness' mean?
    Ans: Knowing something; knowing that something exists and is important; being interested in something.
  • Q: What does 'recklessly' mean?
    Ans: In a way that shows a lack of care about danger and the possible results of your actions.
  • Q: What does 'obvious' mean?
    Ans: Easy to see or understand.
  • Q: What does 'awaken' mean?
    Ans: To wake up; to make somebody wake up.
  • Q: What does 'dumping' mean?
    Ans: The act of getting rid of something that is not wanted.
  • Q: What does 'insomnia' mean?
    Ans: The condition of being unable to sleep.
  • Q: What does 'depletion' mean?
    Ans: The reduction of something by a large amount so that there is not enough left.

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
Grammar — Put the verbs into the correct tense (simple present or present continuous)

  • Q: Look! Sara (go) _____ to meet her aunt.
    Ans: is going
  • Q: On her right hand, Sara (carry) _____ her handbag.
    Ans: is carrying
  • Q: The handbag (be) _____ very beautiful.
    Ans: is

Grammar — Put the verbs into the correct tense (simple past or past perfect)

  • Q: Look! Sara (go) _____ to meet her aunt.
    Ans: went
  • Q: On her right hand, Sara (carry) _____ her handbag.
    Ans: carried
  • Q: The handbag (fall) _____ on the road.
    Ans: had fallen
  • Q: She (return) _____ from her uncle's house yesterday.
    Ans: returned
  • Q: She (intend) _____ to visit all her relatives.
    Ans: had intended

mcqs.q: Look! Sara _____ to meet her aunt. (present continuous)
mcqs.why: The word 'Look!' shows an action happening now, so the present continuous 'is going' is correct, as given in the first tense exercise in the notes.

mcqs.q: On her right hand, Sara _____ her handbag. (present continuous)
mcqs.why: The action is shown happening at the moment of looking, so the present continuous 'is carrying' is the answer given in the notes.

mcqs.q: The handbag _____ very beautiful. (simple present)
mcqs.why: The notes give the simple present form of 'be' as 'is', because the sentence states a general fact about the handbag in the present.

mcqs.q: Sara _____ to meet her aunt. (simple past version of the sentence)
mcqs.why: In the second exercise the same sentence is put in the simple past, and the notes give 'went' as the past form of 'go'.

mcqs.q: On her right hand, Sara _____ her handbag. (simple past)
mcqs.why: The simple past form required by the second exercise and given in the notes is 'carried', the past tense of 'carry'.

mcqs.q: The handbag _____ on the road. (past perfect)
mcqs.why: The notes give 'had fallen' for this item in the simple past or past perfect exercise, using the past perfect form 'had' plus the past participle.

mcqs.q: She _____ from her uncle's house yesterday. (simple past)
mcqs.why: The word 'yesterday' points to a finished past action, so the simple past 'returned' is correct, exactly as given in the notes.

mcqs.q: She _____ to visit all her relatives. (past perfect)
mcqs.why: The notes give 'had intended' for this item, the past perfect form used for an intention formed before another past point.

mcqs.q: Ali _____ football every Sunday. (Choose the correct tense.)
mcqs.why: A regular habit or routine, marked by 'every Sunday', takes the simple present tense, so 'plays' is correct, unlike an action happening now.

mcqs.q: Look! The children _____ in the park right now.
mcqs.why: The signals 'Look!' and 'right now' show an action in progress at this moment, so the present continuous 'are playing' is correct.

mcqs.q: The baby _____ at the moment, so mother cannot rest.
mcqs.why: The phrase 'at the moment' marks an action happening now, which takes the present continuous 'is crying', not the simple present of habit.

mcqs.q: She _____ her homework before her mother came home.
mcqs.why: Finishing the homework happened before the other past action 'her mother came home', so the earlier action takes the past perfect 'had finished'.

mcqs.q: We _____ Lahore last year during the holidays.
mcqs.why: The phrase 'last year' shows a completed action at a definite past time, so the simple past 'visited' is correct.

mcqs.q: The train had already left when we _____ the station.
mcqs.why: The later of the two past actions takes the simple past 'reached', while the earlier leaving is already given in the past perfect 'had left'.

mcqs.q: The sun _____ in the east every morning.
mcqs.why: A general truth and daily routine takes the simple present tense, so 'rises' is correct, just as 'The handbag is very beautiful' states a present fact.

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Writing — Format for Application Writing (with the book's example)

  • Q: Describe the format for application writing given in the book.
    Ans: In the format printed in the book, an application begins with the name and address of the person to whom the application is addressed. Then the subject is written, which gives the reason of the application. After that comes the salutation, such as 'Sir,' or 'Respected Sir,'. The body of the application gives the reasons and mentions the time for which the request is made. The application ends with the closing, the signature of the applicant and the date.
  • Q: Read the example leave application given in the book. What does it say?
    Ans: The Principal, Government High School, Saddar, Peshawar. Subject: Leave Application. Sir/Madam, With due respect, I want to state that I am not in a position to attend the school as I am down with Chickenpox. Since it is a contagious disease, I have been advised quarantine and a few days complete rest by the doctor. Kindly grant me leave for ten days, i.e. 6th Dec 2017 to 16th Dec 2017. Thanking you, Yours obediently, Anum (roll # 123), Class: VIII-B. Dated: 6th Dec 2017.

Writing — Application and Essay

  • Q: A. Write an application to the Deputy Commissioner for financial help.
    Ans: The Deputy Commissioner, Peshawar. Subject: Application for financial help. Respected Sir, With due respect, I beg to state that I am a student of Class VIII. My father is a daily-wage labourer, and last month he fell ill and could not go to work, so our family has no regular income at present. I am a hardworking student and I do not want to leave my studies, but my family cannot pay my school dues and buy my books and uniform. I, therefore, request you to kindly grant me financial help from the deserving students' fund so that I may continue my education. I shall be highly thankful to you for this act of kindness. Thanking you, Yours obediently, Name: _____, Class VIII, Government High School, Peshawar. Dated: _____
  • Q: B. After effective brainstorming, write an essay on the topic 'Let's Stop Pollution' to highlight how everyone must work to stop pollution of the air, water and land, using appropriate transitional words.
    Ans: Pollution is making our air, water and land dirty and dangerous, and it is harming every living thing on earth. Thus, the first duty of every person is to understand that a clean environment is necessary for a healthy life. Smoke from vehicles and factories pollutes the air. Then it causes global warming, acid rain and diseases like lung cancer. Accordingly, we must keep our vehicles fit, plant more trees and stop factories from throwing smoke and waste carelessly. Water is polluted when factories and people dump waste into rivers and ponds. Consequently, fish die and people suffer from cholera, typhoid and dysentery. Therefore, we must never throw garbage into water and must keep our surroundings clean. Land is polluted by over dumping and by the excessive use of fertilizers and pesticides. Henceforth, we should use proper dustbins and disposal systems and avoid plastic bags. In short, pollution can be stopped only when everyone works together. Therefore, let us promise today to keep our air, water and land clean, for a clean Pakistan is a healthy Pakistan.

lessons.title: Practice Activities
lessons.notes_html:
Listening and Speaking — Ask, restate and simplify direction and instructions

  • Q: Make a group and ask, restate and simplify direction and instructions. Give a model exchange.
    Ans: Model exchange: A (asking for directions): 'Excuse me, how can I reach the General Bus Stand from here?' B (restating and simplifying the instruction): 'It is simple. Go straight on this road. Then turn left at the first traffic signal. After that, walk for two minutes, and the bus stand will be on your right.' A: 'So, straight, then left at the signal, and the stand is on the right. Thank you!' Asking short questions, restating the direction in one's own words and breaking it into small, simple steps makes directions and instructions easy to follow.

chapters.title: Unit 9: Someone Who Works Hard To Earn

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Pre-reading — Predict the content by looking at the picture

  • Q: Predict the content by looking at the picture below.
    Ans: The picture shows an old, poor lady sitting on the street with heaps of bananas spread out in front of her for sale. She looks weak and tired, yet she is smiling. From the picture we can predict that the lesson is about a poor street vendor who works hard to earn her living honestly, and about how such hardworking people should be treated with kindness and respect.

Comprehension A — Answer the following questions

  • Q: Q1. Why we should prefer buying from street vendors rather than big stores?
    Ans: We should prefer buying from street vendors because they work hard to earn a small living and often have no other support. A small purchase means very little to us but it is the vendor's whole earning for survival. Big stores charge fixed and often higher prices and do not need our help, while a street vendor depends on every single customer. Buying from them is a simple way of being helpful and supportive to someone who works hard to earn.
  • Q: Q2. How did the author come in touch with the Old Lady?
    Ans: The author was leaving his office when he remembered that his wife had asked him to bring one dozen bananas. Across the road he saw an ill-looking old lady selling fresh bananas on the street. As he was in a hurry to reach home, he went to her and asked her the price. In this way the author came in touch with the Old Lady.
  • Q: Q3. Describe the Old Lady and her problems.
    Ans: The Old Lady was an ill-looking, weak street vendor who sold bananas on the street. Her husband had owned a small fruit shop, but he fell very sick and they had to sell the shop to pay his medical bills, yet he could not survive. She had no child and no relatives who could support her. Now, in her old age, she sells whatever little fruit she can afford to buy, only to survive for what is left of her life.
  • Q: Q4. What was author's opinion about the Old Lady as a street vendor?
    Ans: The author found the Old Lady honest, self-respecting and hardworking. Although she was poor and needed money badly, she refused to take Rs. 50 per dozen and accepted only her fair price of Rs. 36 per dozen, saying she appreciated his kindness. The author felt that such a person, who works hard to earn instead of begging, truly deserves our help and support, and he promised to buy only from her in future.
  • Q: Q5. How did the Old Lady react when he offered her Rs. 50 per dozen for bananas?
    Ans: The Old Lady became very happy at the author's kindness, but she honestly refused to take the extra money. She packed two dozen bananas and said that she could not take Rs. 50 and would take only Rs. 36 per dozen, which was her fair price. She thanked him and said that she appreciated his kindness.
  • Q: Q6. Retell the narrative in the form of a dialogue.
    Ans: Author: What is the price of these bananas? Old Lady: Rs. 37 per dozen, Sir. Author: But the store where I usually buy gives them for Rs. 30 per dozen. Can't you give me for the same price? Old Lady: No Sir, I cannot afford to match that price. I can sell them to you at Rs. 36 per dozen. That is the best I can afford to give you for. Author: Never mind. (Later, at the big grocery shop) Author: I have been buying fruits and vegetables from here for many years. This is a steep price increase. Can't you offer me a better deal for being a loyal customer? Cashier: Sorry Sir, our prices are fixed and we do not bargain. (Back at the Old Lady) Old Lady: Sir, I can't match that price, I won't be able to earn any profit. Author: Don't worry about the price; I will pay you Rs. 50 per dozen! Now, give me 2 dozen. Old Lady: I can't take Rs. 50, but I will take Rs. 36 per dozen. I appreciate your kindness.

Comprehension B — Choose the best option to answer each question

  • Q: 1. The Old Lady was working hard _____.
    Options: to have a competition with the big grocery stores / to survive for what was left of her life / to cover her husband's medical bills / to pay her children's school fee
    Ans: to survive for what was left of her life
  • Q: 2. The big grocery shop did not bargain because _____.
    Options: their prices were fixed / the fruits were fresh and ripe / of competition with other big grocery stores / of advertisement of shops and products
    Ans: their prices were fixed
  • Q: 3. 'I left in my car towards the usual grocery shop'. In this sentence 'I' refers to _____.
    Options: the cashier / the author's colleagues / the author / the Old Lady
    Ans: the author
  • Q: 4. The author did not buy bananas from the big store because _____.
    Options: the bananas were costly / he was in hurry / the bananas were not fresh / he had no money
    Ans: the bananas were costly

Glossary — Word meanings as printed in the unit

  • Q: What does 'dozen' mean?
    Ans: A group of twelve of the same thing.
  • Q: What does 'grocery' mean?
    Ans: Connected with food and other goods sold by a grocer or at a supermarket.
  • Q: What does 'afford' mean?
    Ans: To have enough money or time to be able to buy or to do something.
  • Q: What does 'deaf ear' mean?
    Ans: To ignore or refuse to listen to somebody or something.
  • Q: What does 'attitude' mean?
    Ans: The way that you think and feel about somebody or something; the way that you behave towards somebody or something that shows how you think and feel.
  • Q: What does 'bargain' mean?
    Ans: To argue in an aggressive way and force somebody to agree on the best possible price or arrangement.
  • Q: What does 'instantly' mean?
    Ans: Immediately or without delay.
  • Q: What does 'appreciate' mean?
    Ans: To recognize the good qualities of somebody or something.
  • Q: What does 'liability' mean?
    Ans: The state of being legally responsible for something.
  • Q: What does 'vendor' mean?
    Ans: A person who sells things, for example food or newspapers, usually outside on the street.
  • Q: What does 'steep' mean?
    Ans: Rising or falling quickly, not gradually.
  • Q: What does 'spare' mean?
    Ans: That is not being used or is not needed at the present time; kept in case you need to replace the one you usually use; extra.
  • Q: What does 'courage' mean?
    Ans: The ability to do something dangerous, or to face pain or opposition, without showing fear.
  • Q: What does 'quoted' mean?
    Ans: To tell a customer how much money you will charge them for a job, service or product.

She became happy at his kindness but honestly refused the extra money and took only Rs. 36 per dozen

mcqs.why: She became very happy at his kindness but honestly refused the extra money, packed two dozen bananas and took only her fair price of Rs. 36 per dozen.

mcqs.q: What was the author's opinion about the Old Lady as a street vendor?
options: She was dishonest and charged too much
She was honest, self-respecting and hardworking, and deserved help and support
She should stop selling fruit on the street
She was lucky to have no shop expenses
mcqs.why: The author found her honest, self-respecting and hardworking; although poor, she refused extra money, so he felt she truly deserved help and promised to buy only from her.

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary A — Locate guide and entry words for following in dictionary

  • Q: Locate the guide words and entry word for 'street' in the dictionary.
    Ans: Entry word: street. Meaning: a public road in a town or city, usually with houses or shops on one or both sides. The word is found in the 'str-' section of the dictionary, between guide words such as 'straw' and 'strength', which show the first and last entries on its page.
  • Q: Locate the guide words and entry word for 'banana' in the dictionary.
    Ans: Entry word: banana. Meaning: a long curved fruit with yellow skin and soft sweet flesh. The word is found in the 'ba-' section of the dictionary, between guide words such as 'ball' and 'bank', which show the first and last entries on its page.
  • Q: Locate the guide words and entry words for 'store' in the dictionary.
    Ans: Entry word: store. Meaning: a shop of any size, especially a large one that sells many different types of goods. The word is found in the 'sto-' section of the dictionary, between guide words such as 'stone' and 'storm', which show the first and last entries on its page.
  • Q: Locate the guide words and entry word for 'lady' in the dictionary.
    Ans: Entry word: lady. Meaning: a woman, especially one who is polite and well educated, or a polite way of referring to a woman. The word is found in the 'la-' section of the dictionary, between guide words such as 'lack' and 'lamp', which show the first and last entries on its page.
  • Q: Locate the guide words and entry word for 'colleague' in the dictionary.
    Ans: Entry word: colleague. Meaning: a person that you work with, especially in a profession or a business. The word is found in the 'col-' section of the dictionary, between guide words such as 'collar' and 'collect', which show the first and last entries on its page.
  • Q: Locate the guide words and entry word for 'medical' in the dictionary.
    Ans: Entry word: medical. Meaning: connected with the treatment of illness and injuries, or with medicine. The word is found in the 'me-' section of the dictionary, between guide words such as 'medal' and 'meeting', which show the first and last entries on its page.
  • Q: Locate the guide words and entry word for 'wife' in the dictionary.
    Ans: Entry word: wife. Meaning: the woman that a man is married to. The word is found in the 'wi-' section of the dictionary, between guide words such as 'wide' and 'wild', which show the first and last entries on its page.

Vocabulary B — Find the direct quotations enclosed in quotation marks from the context

  • Q: Find and write the direct quotations enclosed in quotation marks from the narrative.
    Ans: The direct quotations in the narrative are: 1) "But the store where I usually buy from gives them for Rs. 30 per dozen, can't give me for the same price?" 2) "No Sir, I cannot afford to match that price. I can sell them to you at Rs. 36 per dozen. That's best I can afford to give you for." 3) "Never mind." 4) "I have been buying fruits and vegetables from here since many years and this is a steep price increase, can't you offer me a better deal for being a loyal customer?" 5) "Sorry Sir, our prices are fixed and we do not bargain." 6) "Sir, I can't match that price, I won't be able to earn any profit." 7) "Don't worry about the price; I will pay you Rs. 50 per dozen! Now, give me 2 dozen." 8) "I can't take Rs. 50 but I will take Rs. 36 per dozen. I appreciate your kindness." 9) "My husband used to own a small fruit shop but he got very sick..." 10) "Take this and bring more different fruits to sell tomorrow, consider this an advance payment for fruits I will be buying from you." 11) "Do not worry, you are doing well and from tomorrow on, I will only buy bananas from you."

Vocabulary C — Rewrite five sentences from the narrative which have transitive verbs

  • Q: Sentence 1 with a transitive verb from the narrative.
    Ans: "I picked up a good bunch of bananas." The verb 'picked up' is transitive because it takes the object 'a good bunch of bananas'.
  • Q: Sentence 2 with a transitive verb from the narrative.
    Ans: "She was selling fresh bananas on the street." The verb 'was selling' is transitive because it takes the object 'fresh bananas'.
  • Q: Sentence 3 with a transitive verb from the narrative.
    Ans: "I pulled out my wallet and gave her Rs. 500 extra." The verb 'gave' is transitive because it takes the objects 'Rs. 500' and 'her'.
  • Q: Sentence 4 with a transitive verb from the narrative.
    Ans: "I recommended many of my colleagues to buy fruits from the lady." The verb 'recommended' is transitive because it takes the object 'many of my colleagues'.
  • Q: Sentence 5 with a transitive verb from the narrative.
    Ans: "We had to sell his shop to cover his medical bills." The verbs 'sell' and 'cover' are transitive because they take the objects 'his shop' and 'his medical bills'.

Vocabulary D — Write the meaning of the following phrases and use them in sentences

  • Q: give in — meaning and sentence.
    Ans: Meaning: to accept defeat or to agree to something after resisting it. Sentence: The shopkeeper did not want to lower the price, but at last he gave in to the customer's request.
  • Q: give way — meaning and sentence.
    Ans: Meaning: to break or collapse under pressure, or to allow someone else to go first. Sentence: The old bridge gave way under the weight of the loaded truck.
  • Q: give up — meaning and sentence.
    Ans: Meaning: to stop trying to do something. Sentence: The Old Lady never gave up working, even in her old age and weakness.
  • Q: give over — meaning and sentence.
    Ans: Meaning: to hand something over to someone, or to stop doing something. Sentence: He gave over the charge of the shop to his son and retired.
  • Q: give out — meaning and sentence.
    Ans: Meaning: to distribute something, or to stop working. Sentence: The teacher gave out the test papers to all the students.
  • Q: give off — meaning and sentence.
    Ans: Meaning: to produce a smell, light, heat or gas. Sentence: The ripe bananas give off a sweet smell.
  • Q: give back — meaning and sentence.
    Ans: Meaning: to return something to the person it belongs to. Sentence: Please give back my book when you have finished reading it.

Grammar A — Identify each sentence as either simple or compound

  • Q: 1. My dog eats fruit of any kind but she will not eat meat or cheese.
    Ans: Compound sentence. It has two independent clauses, 'My dog eats fruit of any kind' and 'she will not eat meat or cheese', joined by the coordinating conjunction 'but'.
  • Q: 2. The new rug in the living room is beautiful but it does not match the furniture.
    Ans: Compound sentence. It has two independent clauses, 'The new rug in the living room is beautiful' and 'it does not match the furniture', joined by the coordinating conjunction 'but'.
  • Q: 3. Kulsoom applied for a job in accounting at the new medical facility in town.
    Ans: Simple sentence. It has one subject, 'Kulsoom', and one verb, 'applied', and expresses a single complete thought.
  • Q: 4. I went to the store without a list so I bought all junk food.
    Ans: Compound sentence. It has two independent clauses, 'I went to the store without a list' and 'I bought all junk food', joined by the coordinating conjunction 'so'.
  • Q: 5. The flowers in the garden behind our house are in full bloom at this time.
    Ans: Simple sentence. It has one subject, 'The flowers in the garden behind our house', and one verb, 'are', and expresses a single complete thought.

Grammar — Identify whether the sentence is declarative, imperative, interrogative, or exclamatory

  • Q: 1. The tiny sailboat overturned in the gale.
    Ans: Declarative sentence. It makes a statement and ends with a period.
  • Q: 2. Do you like coconut milk?
    Ans: Interrogative sentence. It asks a question and ends with a question mark.
  • Q: 3. The villagers were afraid the volcano would erupt soon.
    Ans: Declarative sentence. It makes a statement and ends with a period.
  • Q: 4. Your perfume stinks!
    Ans: Exclamatory sentence. It expresses a strong feeling and ends with an exclamation mark.
  • Q: 5. Sidra read the barometer every 15 minutes before the storm.
    Ans: Declarative sentence. It makes a statement and ends with a period.

Grammar B — Add the correct ending punctuation. Then write whether the sentence is declarative, imperative, interrogative, or exclamatory

  • Q: 1. Shake the salad dressing for me _____
    Ans: Shake the salad dressing for me. — Imperative sentence. It makes a request and ends with a period.
  • Q: 2. Who threw the baseball through the window _____
    Ans: Who threw the baseball through the window? — Interrogative sentence. It asks a question and ends with a question mark.
  • Q: 3. Get down from there _____
    Ans: Get down from there! — Imperative sentence. It gives a firm command, so it ends with an exclamation mark.
  • Q: 4. Hurrah _____
    Ans: Hurrah! — Exclamatory sentence. It expresses sudden joy and ends with an exclamation mark.
  • Q: 5. The kitten began to nestle against his mother _____
    Ans: The kitten began to nestle against his mother. — Declarative sentence. It makes a statement and ends with a period.

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Writing A — Write down the summary of the narrative 'Someone Who Works Hard to Earn'

  • Q: Write down the summary of the narrative 'Someone Who Works Hard to Earn'.
    Ans: One evening, the narrator was leaving his office when he remembered that his wife had asked for a dozen bananas. He saw an ill-looking old lady selling bananas across the road and tried to bargain her price of Rs. 37 down to Rs. 30, but she could only offer Rs. 36. He left and went to his usual big grocery shop, where he was shocked to find the price was Rs. 50 per dozen, and the cashier flatly refused to bargain. Feeling bad, he returned to the Old Lady and offered her Rs. 50 per dozen for two dozen bananas. The honest lady refused the extra money and took only Rs. 36 per dozen. She told him her sad story: her husband had died after an illness, their shop was sold to pay his medical bills, and she now sold fruit to survive. The narrator gave her Rs. 500 as an advance, promised to buy only from her, and recommended her to his colleagues. With this support, she made a better living. The story teaches us to support those who work hard to earn.

Writing B — Write an essay of about 200 words on 'Dignity of Labour'

  • Q: Write an essay of about 200 words on 'Dignity of Labour', following conventions of essay writing.
    Ans: Dignity of Labour. Every kind of honest work is respectable, and no job is small or mean in itself. This is the dignity of labour. A farmer who grows our food, a cobbler who mends our shoes, a sweeper who keeps our streets clean and a vendor who sells fruit on the roadside all serve society just as a doctor, a teacher or an officer does. Work becomes low only when it is done dishonestly. In many homes, sadly, people look down upon those who work with their hands. They bargain hard with a poor street vendor but pay the fixed price in a big shop without a word. This is unfair. The vendor works in heat and dust from morning to night only to earn a few rupees, and his labour deserves respect, not pity mixed with contempt. Our religion also teaches us that the labourer is a friend of God and that eating from one's own hard work is the best earning. In conclusion, we should respect every worker and every honest profession. A country progresses only when its people value hard work. Let us never feel ashamed of any lawful work, and let us always honour those who work hard to earn.

Writing C — Write a paragraph of comparison and contrast between the Old lady and the cashier of big grocery shop

  • Q: Write a paragraph of comparison and contrast between the Old lady and the cashier of big grocery shop. Use appropriate similes and metaphors for comparison and contrast and connectives of comparison and contrast.
    Ans: The Old Lady and the cashier of the big grocery shop are as different as a kind host and a closed door. Both of them sell fruit and deal with customers, but their behaviour is entirely opposite. The Old Lady is poor and weak, yet she is gentle, polite and honest like a lamp that gives light even while it is burning out. She welcomes the customer warmly, explains her difficulty with respect, and refuses to take even one rupee more than her fair price. On the other hand, the cashier is secure in his big, bright shop, but he is cold and indifferent. He turns a deaf ear to a loyal customer, hides behind fixed prices, and shows no sympathy at all. While the Old Lady's honesty is a garden that wins every heart, the cashier's flat attitude is a wall that pushes customers away. In short, unlike the cashier, the Old Lady proves that true richness lies not in a big shop but in honesty and good manners.

Writing D — Write a short narrative in first person to describe 'A Road Accident'

  • Q: Write a short narrative in first person to describe 'A Road Accident'.
    Ans: Last month, I witnessed a terrible road accident which I can never forget. I was returning home from school in the afternoon when I suddenly heard a loud screech of brakes followed by a heavy crash. I turned around quickly and saw that a speeding motorcycle had hit an old man who was crossing the road near the bazaar. The old man fell down on the road and his bag of vegetables scattered everywhere. For a moment, I stood frozen with fear. Then I ran towards him at once. A small crowd gathered around us. The young motorcyclist, badly frightened, kept saying, "I am sorry, I could not see him in time." We carefully lifted the injured man and made him sit on the footpath. Meanwhile, someone called an ambulance, and fortunately it arrived within a few minutes. I felt relieved when the doctor at the hospital said that the old man had only minor injuries and would recover soon. That day I learnt a painful lesson: a few seconds of hurry on the road can endanger a precious life, so we must always drive slowly and carefully.

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Pre-reading — Look at the pictograph and predict the content of the poem

  • Q: Look at the pictograph and predict the content of the poem.
    Ans: The pictograph shows a happy child thanking Allah because his life is full of blessings. Around him are pictures of good health, eyes, ears, a nose, hands and lips, a loving family, good friends, fresh food, clothes, a place to sleep and a heart that remembers Allah. From these pictures we can predict that the poem will be about thanking Allah for the countless everyday blessings of life, such as health, family, food and a new day to live.

Glossary — Word meanings as printed in the unit

  • Q: What does 'hectic' mean?
    Ans: Very busy; full of activity.
  • Q: What does 'stroll' mean?
    Ans: To walk somewhere in a slow relaxed way.
  • Q: What does 'snuggled' mean?
    Ans: To get into, or to put somebody or something into, a warm comfortable position, especially close to somebody.
  • Q: What does 'duvet' mean?
    Ans: A large cloth bag that is filled with feathers or other soft material and that you have on top of you in bed to keep yourself warm.
  • Q: What does 'bay' mean?
    Ans: A part of the sea, or of a large lake, partly surrounded by a wide curve of the land.
  • Q: What does 'piercing' mean?
    Ans: Affecting you very strongly, especially in a way that causes you pain.
  • Q: What does 'retire' mean?
    Ans: In this poem, to go to rest or to bed at the end of the day. The printed glossary gives the general meaning: to stop doing your job, especially because you have reached a particular age.
  • Q: What does 'prickly' mean?
    Ans: Giving somebody an unpleasant feeling on their skin, like small sharp points pressing against it, as a bed of hay does.
  • Q: What does 'wondrous' mean?
    Ans: Strange, beautiful and impressive.
  • Q: What does 'drift' mean?
    Ans: A slow steady movement from one place to another; in the poem, to fall gently into sleep.

Comprehension A — Answer the following questions

  • Q: Q1. Are we thankful enough to Allah for all our blessings? How?
    Ans: The poem suggests that we are not thankful enough, because we take our blessings for granted and thank Allah only rarely. Every new day, our health, food, family and safety are gifts of Allah, yet we enjoy them without remembering the Giver. We can show true thankfulness by thanking Allah in our prayers every morning and night, by using His blessings in good ways, and by sharing them with others, as the poet does when he falls on his knees and prays with thanks.
  • Q: Q2. Why is life 'wondrous' according to the poet?
    Ans: Life is 'wondrous' according to the poet because it is full of strange, beautiful and impressive blessings. Waking up each morning, hearing birds chirp, watching squirrels play, enjoying sunshine and resting peacefully at night all make life a wonder. Even a busy or difficult day is a gift, so the poet admits that really all is okay and life is a marvel for which we must thank God.
  • Q: Q3. Explain the line 'Before we drift off into dreamland, far, far away-'.
    Ans: This line comes at the end of the poem, when the day is over. 'Drift off' means to fall gently and slowly into sleep, and 'dreamland' is the world of dreams. The poet means that before we fall asleep and enter the faraway world of dreams, we should go down on our knees and thank the Lord for letting us live another precious day.
  • Q: Q4. What is the meaning of the following line? 'Even if my bed be in a barn on a prickly bed of hay,'
    Ans: This line means that the poet is ready to be thankful in every condition, rich or poor. Even if he has no comfortable home or soft bed and has to sleep in a barn, where animals are kept, on a rough and prickly bed of dried grass, he will still thank God. True gratitude does not depend on comfort; it depends on being alive and blessed with another day.
  • Q: Q5. Write down the theme of the poem 'What a Blessing'.
    Ans: The theme of the poem 'What a Blessing' is gratitude to God for the gift of life and its everyday blessings. In every stanza the poet repeats that waking up to a new day is itself a blessing, whether the day is busy or restful, cold or sunny, comfortable or hard. The poem teaches us to notice the small gifts of nature and daily life, to be content in every condition, and to thank the Lord every day for letting us live another precious day.
  • Q: Q6. How does the poet express his gratitude to God in the second stanza?
    Ans: In the second stanza, the poet expresses his gratitude by saying that waking up is a blessing whatever the weather is like. Even on a cold day, when the sky is dark and grey and he is snuggled up in bed under his fluffy duvet, he is thankful. And when the first light appears over a beautiful clear bay and the sun touches his heart with a piercing little ray, he ends the stanza with the refrain of thanks: 'Thank you LORD for letting me live another precious day.'

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary — Deduce the meaning of the following words from the text

  • Q: What does 'blessing' mean in the poem?
    Ans: A gift or favour from God; something good that brings happiness and for which we should be thankful. In the poem, waking up to a new day is itself a blessing.
  • Q: What does 'chirping' mean in the poem?
    Ans: Making short, sharp, high sounds, as small birds do when they sing in the morning. The poet hears the birds chirping as they go on their way.
  • Q: What does 'merry' mean in the poem?
    Ans: Happy and cheerful. The birds go happily on their way, and the poet feels merry at the start of the new day.
  • Q: What does 'crazy' mean in the poem?
    Ans: Very busy, wild and full of hurry; here it describes a day full of rush and activity for which the poet still feels thankful.
  • Q: What does 'stream' mean in the poem?
    Ans: A small, narrow river or flow of water. The poet speaks of taking a walk by the stream.
  • Q: What does 'precious' mean in the poem?
    Ans: Very valuable and loved; the poet calls each new day precious because life itself is a precious gift of God.
  • Q: What does 'fluffy' mean in the poem?
    Ans: Soft, light and thick, like feathers or wool; the poet lies snuggled under a fluffy duvet on a cold morning.
  • Q: What does 'ray' mean in the poem?
    Ans: A thin beam of light or heat from the sun. The sun touches the poet's heart with a piercing little ray at sunrise.
  • Q: What does 'gay' mean in the poem?
    Ans: Happy and cheerful; the poet retires at the end of the day happy and gay, satisfied with the day he has lived.
  • Q: What does 'hay' mean in the poem?
    Ans: Dried grass that is used as food or bedding for animals; the poet is ready to sleep even on a bed of hay in a barn.
  • Q: What does 'admit' mean in the poem?
    Ans: To accept the truth and agree that something is true; the poet admits that really all is okay because of God's blessings.
  • Q: What does 'pray' mean in the poem?
    Ans: To speak to God, to thank Him or to ask Him for something; at night the poet goes down on his knees and prays with thanks before sleeping.

Vocabulary A — Find words in the poem which mean the same as

  • Q: Find the word in the poem which means the same as 'God sent'.
    Ans: The word in the poem is 'blessing'. The poet repeats, 'What a blessing it is to wake up every single day,' meaning a gift sent by God.
  • Q: Find the word in the poem which means the same as 'allowing'.
    Ans: The word in the poem is 'letting', in the refrain 'Thank you Lord for letting me live another precious day.' Letting means allowing someone to do something.
  • Q: Find the word in the poem which means the same as 'cheerful'.
    Ans: The words in the poem are 'merry' and 'gay'. The birds go on their 'merry way', and the poet retires at the end of the day 'happy and gay'; both words mean cheerful.
  • Q: Find the word in the poem which means the same as 'valuable'.
    Ans: The word in the poem is 'precious', in the line 'Thank you Lord for letting me live another precious day.' Precious means very valuable.

    Ans: the

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Writing — Paraphrase and Summary

  • Q: A. Paraphrase the 2nd stanza of the poem.
    Ans: In the second stanza, the poet says that it is a blessing to wake up every morning, whatever the weather may be. If the day is cold and the sky is dark and grey, he is still thankful as he lies snuggled warmly in bed under his soft, fluffy duvet. And if the day begins with first light appearing over a beautiful, clear bay, and the rays of the sun touch his heart, he is equally thankful. In every condition he thanks the Lord for letting him live another precious day.
  • Q: B. Write the summary of the poem.
    Ans: The poem 'What a Blessing' is a song of thankfulness. In every stanza the poet repeats that waking up to a new day is itself a great blessing of God. He thanks the Lord for the beauty of nature, the chirping of birds, the playing squirrels, a walk by the stream, the warmth of his bed on a cold morning and the light of the sun over the bay. He is ready to do his planned work in the day and to retire happy at night, even if his bed is a prickly bed of hay in a barn. Surrounded by so many blessings, he admits that life is wondrous and all is okay, and before falling asleep he kneels down and prays, thanking the Lord for letting him live another precious day.

mcqs.why: The paraphrase describes first light over a beautiful clear bay and the rays of the sun touching the poet's heart.

options: Only the sea and the moon

mcqs.why: The summary lists the beauty of nature, chirping birds, playing squirrels and a walk by the stream among the blessings thanked for.

mcqs.why: The summary says he is ready to do his planned work and retire happy at night, even if his bed is a prickly bed of hay in a barn.

options: That life is wondrous and all is okay

mcqs.why: The summary states that surrounded by blessings he admits life is wondrous and really all is okay, echoing the poem's own admission.

options: He kneels down and prays, thanking the Lord for letting him live another precious day
mcqs.why: The summary ends with the poet kneeling and praying before sleep, thanking the Lord for letting him live another precious day.

options: Cold day — dark grey sky and fluffy duvet

mcqs.why: The paraphrase pairs the cold day with a dark grey sky and being snuggled under a fluffy duvet, while the clear bay belongs to the fine morning.

options: A song of thankfulness for a new day and all of God's blessings
mcqs.why: The notes begin the summary by calling the poem a song of thankfulness, repeating thanks for a new day and God's many blessings.

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Pre-reading

  • Q: Q1. Do you know what is peaceful coexistence?
    Ans: Peaceful coexistence means living together with other people in peace and harmony. It means respecting everyone despite differences of religion, colour, social class or creed, forgiving those who wrong us, and helping others in the hour of need instead of quarrelling with them.
  • Q: Q2. What are the ways to live in peace with others?
    Ans: We can live in peace with others by respecting everyone, forgiving the person who wrongs us, and doing him well whenever possible. We should not interfere in the affairs of others, should turn a deaf ear to insults instead of reacting adversely, and should help others selflessly in the hour of need, as Islam teaches us.

Glossary — Word Meanings

  • Q: What does 'inferred' mean?
    Ans: To reach an opinion or decide that something is true on the basis of information that is available.
  • Q: What does 'injunction' mean?
    Ans: An official order given by a court which demands that something must or must not be done. In the lesson, the injunctions of Islam mean the teachings and commands of Islam.
  • Q: What does 'advocate' mean?
    Ans: To support something publicly.
  • Q: What does 'disparaging' mean?
    Ans: Suggesting that somebody or something is not important or valuable.
  • Q: What does 'adversely' mean?
    Ans: In a way that is negative and unpleasant and not likely to produce a good result.
  • Q: What does 'ridicule' mean?
    Ans: To make fun of somebody in an unkind way; mocking or insulting laughter. Note: the meaning printed against 'ridicule' in the book repeats the meaning of 'adversely' by mistake.
  • Q: What does 'devotion' mean?
    Ans: Great love, care and support for somebody or something.
  • Q: What does 'exhausted' mean?
    Ans: Very tired.

Comprehension A — Answer the following questions

  • Q: Q1. What does the story of Hassan Basri teach us?
    Ans: The story of Hazrat Hassan Basri teaches us to forgive those who insult us and to maintain a respectful attitude towards them instead of reacting adversely. Hazrat Hassan Basri forgave his fellow travellers who ridiculed him for his simple appearance during a sea voyage, and ultimately they realized their mistake and asked for forgiveness. It teaches us that when we respect others, we are respected in return.
  • Q: Q2. Why did the university students make fun of Asfandyar?
    Ans: The university students thought Asfandyar was different from them and found his simplicity strange, so they often ridiculed him. There was a group of students who thought themselves above the rest, and they continued to pick on Asfandyar.
  • Q: Q3. Why did Asfandyar decide to look after Jack in the hospital? Do you agree with his decision? Give reasons for your answer.
    Ans: Jack had fallen seriously ill and was all alone in the hospital. His parents lived very far away and it would take a few days for them to get there, and his own friends only came for a few minutes and did not stay to look after him. Asfandyar decided to look after Jack because, as a Muslim, he considered it his duty to care for his sick mate in the hour of need. Yes, I agree with his decision, because helping a person in trouble, even one who has been rude to us, is true humanity and the real teaching of peaceful coexistence.
  • Q: Q4. What role can we all play in promoting peaceful coexistence with everyone around us?
    Ans: We can all promote peaceful coexistence by respecting everyone around us regardless of their social class, religion, colour or creed. We should forgive those who wrong us and do them well whenever possible, especially in the hour of need. We should never ridicule anyone, should not interfere in the affairs of others, and should live with others in peace and harmony, as our religion teaches us.
  • Q: Q5. What is the theme of the story 'The Devoted Mate'?
    Ans: The theme of the story is peaceful coexistence. It teaches us to live with others in peace and harmony, to respect all humankind, to forgive the transgressor and to help him in the hour of need. It also shows that selfless devotion and good behaviour win hearts and can turn a rude person into a good friend, as happened with Jack.
  • Q: Q6. What are the benefits of living peacefully?
    Ans: Living peacefully creates love, trust and harmony in society. People respect us in return, as the saying in the lesson tells us. Enemies and rude people change their attitude and become friends, just as Jack became the good friend of Asfandyar. Everyone can study and work without fear or disturbance, and this peaceful life also pleases Allah, because Islam advocates respect of all humankind.
  • Q: Q7. Why did Jack's attitude towards Asfandyar change?
    Ans: When Jack recovered, his father told him the whole story of the selfless services of Asfandyar, who had nursed him day and night for three days. He also told him that his dear friends had hardly come to the hospital to enquire after his health. Jack felt ashamed of how he had behaved with Asfandyar and how he had laughed at him, so he asked for forgiveness and offered him a hand of friendship.
  • Q: Q8. Have you ever helped anybody in your life? How?
    Ans: Yes, I have helped others many times. Once my class fellow fell ill before the examinations and missed many lessons. I visited his home every evening, shared my notebooks with him and carefully explained all the missed lessons to him. In this way he recovered his loss, appeared in the examinations with confidence and passed with good marks.
  • Q: Q9. How did Jack's father express his feelings towards Asfandyar?
    Ans: Jack's father was very impressed by the sincere devotion of Asfandyar. He advised Asfandyar to take rest, as he looked dead tired and exhausted, and he thanked him warmly for his selfless services. Later, he told Jack the whole story of how Asfandyar had cared for him day and night, while Jack's own friends had hardly come to see him.

Comprehension B — Complete the cloze paragraph

  • Q: One day Jack, suddenly _____ seriously ill.
    Ans: fell
  • Q: His condition _____ from bad to worse, and a point came that he lost consciousness.
    Ans: grew
  • Q: His condition grew from bad to worse, _____ a point came that he lost consciousness.
    Ans: and
  • Q: His condition grew from bad to worse, and a point came that _____ lost consciousness.
    Ans: he
  • Q: The university _____ shifted him to a hospital and informed his parents.
    Ans: administration
  • Q: The university administration shifted him to a _____ and informed his parents.
    Ans: hospital
  • Q: _____ was very concerned for Jack as he knew that Jack's parents lived very far and it would take a few days for them to get there.
    Ans: Asfandyar
  • Q: Asfandyar was very concerned for _____ as he knew that Jack's parents lived very far.
    Ans: Jack
  • Q: Asfandyar was very concerned for Jack as he knew that _____ parents lived very far.
    Ans: Jack's
  • Q: Asfandyar knew that Jack's parents lived very far _____ it would take a few days for them to get there.
    Ans: and
  • Q: It would take a _____ days for them to get there.
    Ans: few
  • Q: It would take a few days for them to _____ there.
    Ans: get

Vocabulary A — Use dictionary to find the meaning of the following words. Also find guide and entry words for the following words

  • Q: What are guide words and entry words in a dictionary?
    Ans: Guide words are the two words printed at the top of a dictionary page. The first guide word is the first entry word on that page and the second guide word is the last entry word on that page. An entry word is the word that is looked up and explained in the dictionary. To find a word quickly, we first locate the page whose two guide words come before and after our word in alphabetical order.
  • Q: What does 'concerned' mean?
    Ans: Worried and feeling concern about something; in the lesson, Asfandyar was very concerned for Jack, that is, he was worried about Jack's health.
  • Q: What does 'selfless' mean?
    Ans: Thinking more about the needs and wishes of other people than about your own; unselfish. Asfandyar served the ailing Jack day and night selflessly.
  • Q: What does 'pledge' mean?
    Ans: A serious promise or agreement. In the lesson, Jack pledged that from then onwards he would respect everyone.
  • Q: What does 'regain' mean?
    Ans: To get back something that was lost. In the lesson, Jack fully regained consciousness after a few days.
  • Q: What does 'patient' mean?
    Ans: A person who is receiving medical treatment in a hospital. In the lesson, Jack is the patient whom Asfandyar nursed carefully for three days.
  • Q: What does 'simplicity' mean?
    Ans: The quality of being simple and plain, without show or pride. The students found Asfandyar's simplicity strange and ridiculed him for it.
  • Q: What does 'recover' mean?
    Ans: To become well again after an illness. In the lesson, after a few days Jack's health began to recover.

Vocabulary B — Put the following sentences in sequential order and summarize the story

  • Q: Put the sentences in sequential order.
    Ans: The correct order is: 1. His mother told him a story of Hazrat Hassan Basri who was a famous Muslim saint. 2. When Asfandyar started his studies in the university his worse fears came true. 3. Our religion teaches us to live with others in peace and harmony. 4. His condition grew from bad to worse, and a point came that he lost consciousness. 5. He had been taking care of the patient for three days, giving him medicines on time and nursing him carefully. 6. Asfandyar replied that as a Muslim it was his duty to care for his sick friend.
  • Q: Summarize the story 'The Devoted Mate'.
    Ans: Asfandyar, a very diligent Pakistani student, went to study in a big university in a foreign country. Before his departure, his mother told him the story of Hazrat Hassan Basri, who forgave the fellow travellers who ridiculed him, and advised Asfandyar to respect all his fellow students. At the university, many students ridiculed Asfandyar for his simplicity, but he never reacted adversely and remained focused on his studies. His roommate Jack was among the rude students and hardly ever spoke to him. One day Jack fell seriously ill and was shifted to a hospital, all alone, because his parents lived very far away. Asfandyar nursed him day and night selflessly for three days, giving him medicines on time, while Jack's own friends only came for a few minutes. When Jack recovered and learnt the whole story from his father, he felt ashamed, asked for forgiveness and offered Asfandyar a hand of friendship. Both became good friends, and Jack pledged to respect everyone and live peacefully with others.

Grammar — Classify the following adjectives according to different types and write them in the correct column

  • Q: Which of the given adjectives are adjectives of quality?
    Ans: Quality: tasty, old, new, pretty, bony, stout. These adjectives describe the nature or kind of a noun, for example a tasty dish and a pretty girl.
  • Q: Which of the given adjectives are adjectives of quantity?
    Ans: Quantity: little, less. These adjectives tell us the amount, or the approximate amount, of the noun they describe.
  • Q: Which of the given adjectives are adjectives of size?
    Ans: Size: long, massive, bulky, broad, small, slim. These adjectives describe how large or small someone or something is, that is, the amount of space occupied.
  • Q: Which of the given adjectives are adjectives of origin?
    Ans: Origin: English, Chinese, Mexican. These adjectives describe where a person, place or thing has come from.
  • Q: Which of the given adjectives are adjectives of shape?
    Ans: Shape: spherical, round, circle (circular), oblong, square. These adjectives describe the shape of nouns or objects.
  • Q: Which of the given adjectives are adjectives of colour?
    Ans: Colour: dark, silver, red, orange, golden. These adjectives describe the colour of nouns or objects. Note: the word 'silver' is printed twice in the book's list; it is counted once here.

Grammar — Degrees of Adjectives: Complete the following sentences using the appropriate form of the adjective in brackets. Also insert 'the' and 'than' to show comparison

  • Q: She is _____ _____ her sister. (pretty)
    Ans: prettier than
  • Q: Suraya is _____ _____ intelligent girl in the class. (intelligent)
    Ans: the most
  • Q: Russia is _____ _____ country in the world. (large)
    Ans: the largest
  • Q: This is _____ _____ interesting book I have ever read. (interesting)
    Ans: the most
  • Q: It was _____ _____ memorable trip. (memorable)
    Ans: the most

Grammar — Absolute Adjectives: Pick out absolute adjectives in the following sentences

  • Q: 1. She wore a perfect diamond ring on her finger. Pick out the absolute adjective.
    Ans: The absolute adjective is 'perfect'. A ring is either perfect or not perfect; it cannot be more or less perfect.
  • Q: 2. He has a unique name. Pick out the absolute adjective.
    Ans: The absolute adjective is 'unique'. Something unique is one of its kind and cannot be graded as more unique or less unique.
  • Q: 3. He's completely fascinated by history. Pick out the absolute adjective.
    Ans: The absolute adjective is 'fascinated', modified by the absolute adverb 'completely'. A person is either fascinated or not; we cannot say more fascinated in degrees.
  • Q: 4. This exercise is absolutely impossible. Pick out the absolute adjective.
    Ans: The absolute adjective is 'impossible', modified by 'absolutely'. A thing is either possible or impossible; it cannot be more impossible.
  • Q: 5. That film is really terrifying. Don't go and see it on your own. Pick out the absolute adjective.
    Ans: The absolute adjective is 'terrifying'. In this exercise it is used as a complete, ungraded quality of the film, strengthened by 'really'.

Grammar — Varying Position of Adjectives: Rearrange the following sentences in the correct order of position of adjectives

  • Q: Rearrange: pencils two got I've orange
    Ans: I've got two orange pencils.
  • Q: Rearrange: got you phone a have mobile new
    Ans: Have you got a new mobile phone?
  • Q: Rearrange: got red blanket a Mateen
    Ans: Mateen got a red blanket.
  • Q: Rearrange: haven't got a classroom we big
    Ans: We haven't got a big classroom.
  • Q: Rearrange: the following read line carefully
    Ans: Read the following line carefully.
  • Q: Rearrange: She silver the in a ring box put
    Ans: She put the silver ring in a box.
  • Q: Rearrange: easy is the solution no to problem there
    Ans: There is no easy solution to the problem.

Grammar — Formation of Adjectives from Nouns and Verbs: Form adjectives from the following nouns and verbs. Also use the adjectives in sentences of your own

  • Q: Form an adjective from 'hero' and use it in a sentence.
    Ans: Adjective: heroic. Sentence: The heroic soldier saved the wounded people without caring for his own life.
  • Q: Form an adjective from 'talk' and use it in a sentence.
    Ans: Adjective: talkative. Sentence: My younger sister is very talkative and keeps chatting with everyone all day.
  • Q: Form an adjective from 'wind' and use it in a sentence.
    Ans: Adjective: windy. Sentence: It was a cold and windy day, so we stayed inside the house.
  • Q: Form an adjective from 'beauty' and use it in a sentence.
    Ans: Adjective: beautiful. Sentence: The beautiful garden was full of colourful flowers in spring.
  • Q: Form an adjective from 'use' and use it in a sentence.
    Ans: Adjective: useful. Sentence: A dictionary is a very useful book for every student of English.
  • Q: Form an adjective from 'like' and use it in a sentence.
    Ans: Adjective: likeable. Sentence: Asfandyar is a likeable young man because of his respectful and selfless nature.
  • Q: Form an adjective from 'hill' and use it in a sentence.
    Ans: Adjective: hilly. Sentence: Murree is a hilly area that remains cool even in summer.

Grammar — Adjective Phrases: Identify the adjective phrases in the following sentences

  • Q: 1. Have you ever seen an elephant with a white skin? Identify the adjective phrase.
    Ans: The adjective phrase is 'with a white skin'. It modifies the noun 'elephant'.
  • Q: 2. He was wearing a crown made of gold. Identify the adjective phrase.
    Ans: The adjective phrase is 'made of gold'. It modifies the noun 'crown'.
  • Q: 3. There I met a girl with blue eyes. Identify the adjective phrase.
    Ans: The adjective phrase is 'with blue eyes'. It modifies the noun 'girl'.
  • Q: 4. Wild beasts in small cages are a sorry sight. Identify the adjective phrase.
    Ans: The adjective phrase is 'in small cages'. It modifies the noun 'wild beasts'.
  • Q: 5. A man with a long beard came to see me. Identify the adjective phrase.
    Ans: The adjective phrase is 'with a long beard'. It modifies the noun 'man'.

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Writing A — Write your own story on the same theme using the following beginning

  • Q: Write your own story on the same theme (peaceful coexistence and helping others in the hour of need), beginning: 'Once on my way back home I came across my class fellow Adil. He had an accident and...'
    Ans: Once on my way back home I came across my class fellow Adil. He had an accident and was lying badly injured beside his broken bicycle. A small crowd had gathered around him, but nobody was ready to take him to the hospital. Adil was not my close friend; in fact, he often teased me at school and laughed at my old bag and worn-out shoes. For a moment I remembered all his insults, but then I remembered my mother's words that we should help everyone in the hour of need, even those who have wronged us. At once I hired a rickshaw with my pocket money, lifted Adil into it carefully and took him to the nearest hospital. I stayed with him bravely until the doctor had bandaged his wounds and his worried parents arrived. His mother thanked me again and again with tears in her eyes. The next week, when Adil returned to school, he came straight to me, asked for my forgiveness for all his teasing and offered me a hand of friendship. From that day onwards we became the best of friends, and I learnt that kindness and forgiveness can change even a rude heart.

Writing B — With the help of the mind map below, write the character sketch of Asfandyar from the story 'The Devoted Mate'

  • Q: Write the character sketch of Asfandyar, covering his nature, motives, actions and emotional responses.
    Ans: Asfandyar is the central character of the story 'The Devoted Mate'. By nature he is a very diligent, simple, respectful and selfless young student. He never interferes in the affairs of others and always remains focused on his studies, which is why his teachers admire him for his hard work and respectful attitude. His motives are pure and religious: he follows the true injunctions of Islam, remembers the story of Hazrat Hassan Basri told by his mother, and believes that it is his duty as a Muslim to forgive the transgressor and help him in the hour of need. His actions prove his character. Although Jack, his roommate, ridiculed him and hardly ever spoke to him, Asfandyar nursed the seriously ill Jack day and night for three days in the hospital, giving him medicines on time and not leaving his side until Jack's father arrived. His emotional responses are always calm and controlled: he is never discouraged by insults, turns a deaf ear to the insulting attitude of others, feels genuinely concerned for his sick mate, and politely refuses to take rest even when he is dead tired and exhausted. In short, Asfandyar is a model of peaceful coexistence, devotion and forgiveness.
